Heb. *weeks of ordinances,* or, *appointments of harvest:* whence one of the Jewish doctors would have some respect had to the two ordinances, made for their harvest oblations; the one for the *sheaf,* Lev. 23. 10. the other for the *loaves,* Lev. 23. 17. another to two requisites in harvest times; fair weather to reap, and a good wind to winnow. But the former is wholly here impertinent, the latter overcurious. Their harvest time for corn, was within the compass commonly of two months, half *Nisan,* all *Sivan,* and half *Iyar:* but he says rather *weeks,* than *months,* or *days;* in reference to those *seven weeks,* between those two solemn feasts of *Pasch,* and *Pentecost,* Lev. 23. 15. Num. 28. 20. Deut. 16. 9. (whence the latter of them is called *the feast of weeks,* Exo. 34. 22. Deut. 16. 10, 16.) within which it was the most part usually got in; in this regard they were enjoined at the *Pasch,* at which time they began to put sickle to their corn, Deut. 16. 9. to bring for an oblation to the Lord, a certain quantity of corn; that is, as it is generally deemed, of barley: because that was sooner ripe with them, as in Egypt also, Exod. 9. 31, 32. than wheat, Ruth 2. 23. whether in the ear, or beaten out, is questioned; because the term used in the law is ambiguous, signifying as well a *sheaf* of corn, as a certain measure of grain, or meal: nor was it lawful for them to eat any bread, or parched corn, or green ear of that year's grain, until this offering had been tendered, Lev. 23. 14, 15. and at *Pentecost,* (from the number of days, making up those weeks, Lev. 23. 16. so termed, Act. 2. 1. 1 Cor. 16. 8.) they were to bring two loaves made of fine flour, of wheat, as it is generally deemed, being their wheat harvest then begun, and in its height, or heat, if not well near done; for a *tribute,* as it is termed, Deut. 16. 10. or, in nature of their *first fruits,* as it is styled, Lev. 23. 17. in regard whereof, is the first day of that festival, called *the day of the first fruits,* Num. 28. 20. Some of our interpreters of chief note here, step out of the common road; some reading the words here; *that keepeth with us the oaths of the statutes of harvest;* as having reference to the *oath,* that God took for the continuance of harvest in its due season, Gen. 8. 22. but of any *oaths* much less, as here, there is no mention there. Others rendering them, *the sevens,* and *the statutes of harvest:* and by the former, understanding the seventh year, wherein they were forbidden to till, Lev. 25. 4, 7. by the latter, the blessing that God promised to give in those years, Lev. 25. 20, 22. but I find not the word of *sevens,* or, *weeks,* anywhere so used; and it seems to distract the text too much: as for the ancient Greek and old Latin, who in stead of *weeks,* here read and render *fulness,* they are too too apparently out of the way, supposing it to come from a root that signifies *to satiate,* which this has no affinity with, nor has that any place here: which gross mistake of our Popish writers endeavor to salve, in stead of discovering, as they might better have done; the ground of their error.

**Verse 25.** *{Your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withholden good things from you}* Heb. *good from you;* as Isa. 55. 2. This is the true cause why your rains have been restrained, ch. 3. 3. If there be any restraint of God's blessings, it is by reason of man's sin, Psal. 107. 17, 34. Isa. 59. 1, 2.

**Verse 26.** *{For among my people are found wicked men; they lye in wait as he that setteth snares, they set a trap, they catch men}* Or, *that lye in wait,* or, *watch,* or, *pry* each of them; (a defect of the relative, as ver. 7, 17. and a change of the number, as Joel 1. 20.) *as when fowlers couch themselves;* (the particle including a twofold notion, as Isa. 54. 9. & 64. 2. vers. 25.) *they set a snare,* or, *a gin, to take men:* as, *rose and warred,* for, *rose to war,* Josh. 24. 9. *rose early corrupted,* for, *rose early to corrupt,* Zeph. 3. 7. *know not give not,* for, *know not* how *to give,* Job 32. 22. So also Eccl. 8. 1.

*{are found}* Or, *are to be found;* for, *to be,* as Esther 1. 5. Luke 17. 18.

*{lay wait}* Or, *watch,* or, *pry;* for so the word properly signifies, Hos. 11. 7. whence *enemies* are called *priers,* or, *watchers;* because they eye men to do them some mischief, Psa. 5. 8. & 27. 11. & 54. 7. & 56. 2. & 59. 10. & 92. 11. See of Saul the like, 1 Sam. 18. 11.

*{as he that setteth snares}* Or, *as fowlers;* or, *as when fowlers* (so the word is ever taken, Psa. 91. 3. Prov. 6. 5. Hos. 9. 8. never for *a snare) couch,* or, *lie still* and quiet; as those do that lie in wait: Heb. *as,* or, *according to fowlers in couching;* for the verb in the form here used, is never found in a transitive notion, ever in an immanent. So it is used of the waters of the deluge; *the waters were abated,* or, *allayed;* fell, and began to be low, Gen. 8. 1. and *the Kings anger was laid,* or, *appeased,* Esther 2. 1. & 7. 10. and in the transitive form, *that thou maist still their murmuring,* Num. 17. 10. they lie in wait to catch men, as fowlers do to take fowl, Prov. 1. 11, 17, 18. See also Psal. 10. 8, 10. in which place, a word somewhat like that here; as well in sound, as in sense, is of the like use, as also, Job 38. 40.

*{they set a trap}* Or, *gin,* or, *snare:* the word properly signifies *perdition,* or, *destruction,* Exod. 12. 13. 2 Chr. 20. 23. Ezek. 21. 31. in the next place, *a gin,* or, *snare,* set on purpose to work destruction; in which notion it is here alone found: a learned late writer renders it, *a pit;* and true it is that a word somewhat near it, and as some think, of the same family with it, is used sometime for *corruption,* sometime for a *pit,* Psal. 16. 10. & 94. 13. & 103. 4. Prov. 26. 27. as also that *pitfalls* are made to take birds; and both pits dug, and snares laid in pits to catch other creatures, Psa. 7. 15. & 9. 15. & 35. 7. but that will not fit well here; for, *to set a pit,* carries no good sense; rather, as most render it, *they set traps,* or *gins,* or, *snares;* (for the word is here collectively used) *to catch men;* either to spoil them, or slay them, or both, Prov. 1. 11, 13, 16, 19. So set Jezebel a snare for Naboth, 1 King. 21. and Saul divers for David, though none of them took; See 1 Sam. 18. 17, 21, 25. & 19. 1, 11, 17, 20. & 23. 7, 9, 14, 22, 23.

**Verse 27.** *{As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit}* *A cage,* or, *a coop;* for it is (as the Jewish masters tell us) a receptacle made of boards, wherein fowlers and poulterers used to keep and fat their fowl: the fowler's cage or coop, of whom before, v. 26. and it may signify as well one made of twigs, as of boards; for it is used also for *a maund,* or, *a basket,* Amos 8. 1, 2.

*{their houses full of deceit}* Of goods gotten by *deceit;* by such wiles and devices as they ensnare men withal: as, *falsehood,* for goods got by *falsehood,* Esay 28. 15. *labor;* for goods gotten by painstaking, ch. 3. 24. See Mic. 6. 10. Zeph. 1. 9.

*{therefore are they become great, and waxen rich}* Or, *thereby;* or, *by such means.* Heb. *for so.*

**Verse 28.** *{They are waxen fat}* Fat; that is, wealthy, Psal. 22. 29. Hab. 1. 10. or *corpulent,* being full fed, Psa. 73. 7. & 119. 70. See v. 7. Deu. 32. 15.

*{they shine}* Or, *they are slick,* or, smooth; without wrinkles, as full and fat bodies use to be: so the noun hence deduced, (for the verb is nowhere else found) as *polished,* or, *smooth ivory,* Cant. 5. 14. and, *polished,* or, *smooth iron,* Ezek. 27. 19. for that is all the stock of it.

*{yea, they overpass the deeds of the wicked}* According to this Version the meaning should be; they go beyond the very heathen themselves in wickedness, See Chap. 2. 33. Ezek. 5. 6, 7. and so the Jewish commenters also understand the text. The ancient Greek renders it, *they pass by judgment;* which would suit well with what follows, if the words would bear it, but either mangles the text, or forces it overmuch. The Chaldee, *They transgress the words of the Law, they do evil:* and much to the same effect, the old Latin; *they do wickedly pass by my words:* but they both also put in, what is not in the text. The Hebrew is word for word, *they pass by words,* or, *matters of evil; words,* or, *matters, of evil,* is no other than *evil things,* Psal. 65. 3. as, *words,* or, *matters, of fastings, and a cry;* for, the *fasts and cries* themselves. So Chap. 7. 4, 8, 22. this some of the Rabbines expound, when any evil either is menaced, or befalls them for the evil they do; they pass it, or, put it by, and do the evil for all that; as vers. 3. Some of ours, whom I concur with, *they pass by evils;* they escape those evil occurrents of penalty and judgment, wherewith others are surprised, as Psal. 73. 5. Howbeit, a learned late writer, understands it of persons, *in bad case, sad,* or *afflicted;* as the word *evil,* is oft used, Gen. 41. 4. Lev. 27. 10, 33. Prov. 15. 15. as if the meaning were; *they pass by the matters,* or, the causes of such, refusing to meddle with them: which though it would suit well with what follows, yet seems here somewhat forced.

*{they judge not the cause, the cause of the fatherless}* *Cause:* Heb. *judgment,* as Deut. 17. 8. chap. 22. 16. & 30. 13. *the cause,* I say, *of the fatherless;* or, *orphan;* either they refuse to hear it, Esay 1. 23. or, if they do, they right them not, but wrong them rather, Zech. 7. 10. Hereby it appears, that what was before said, was against those principally intended, that were in place of judicature; yet not excluding others also, whom for bribes, those great ones backed and bore out; See Esay 1. 23. Mic. 7. 2, 3. Zeph. 3. 3, 4.

*{yet they prosper.}* Heb. *and,* as vers. 10, 22. They thrive with, or notwithstanding, their wickedness: as Job 21. 7, 15. Psal. 73. 3, 12. chap. 12. 1, 2. Hab. 1. 3, 4. Zech. 11. 5. or, as the words may well be read, *that they might prosper:* for so also is the copulative frequently used, Josh. 24. 9. Esay 10. 19. & 11. 3. & 13. 2. & 41. 22. & 63. 2. See v. 22. they do not execute judgment and justice, that they might prosper through God's blessing upon them for the same, ch. 22. 15, 16.

*{and the right of the needy they do not judge.}* *The right,* or *the cause,* as before. Heb. *the judgment:* another word of the same notion with the former. So Exo. 23. 6. Job 31. 13.

**Verse 29.** *{Shall I not visit for these things? saith the LORD; shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?}* Or, *Should I not?* see vers. 9. I might, otherwise, seem to be neither just nor merciful. See Exod. 22. 22, 24, 27. Luke 18. 2, 8. James 2. 23.

**Verse 30.** *{A wonderful and horrible thing is committed in the land.}* Heb. *a stupendous;* such a thing as a man would be astonished at: as, *Be astonished, O heavens,* chap. 2. 12. for from thence the word comes: and *an abominable thing,* not an *horrid,* as some; such as may make a man's *hair* stand an end: for it comes not from that root, though they be very near: the roots differ, as Shibboleth, and Sibboleth, Judg. 12. 6. though some would have that diversity oft-times disregarded, see on v. 8. but *a vile, filthy, abominable* thing, such an one as a man would loathe and abhor: it is used of those *figs,* said to be so bad, that there was no eating of them, ch. 29. 17. So ch. 18. 13. & 23. 14. Hos. 6. 10.

*{in the land}* Or, *in this land:* for the article here has his force.

**Verse 31.** *{The Prophets prophesy falsely;}* Heb. *in,* or *by,* or *with a falsehood,* or *a lie:* as ch. 14. 14. & 20. 6. & 23. 25, 26. Ezek. 13. 6. Either they prophesy *in Baal's* name, ch. 2. 8. or they prophesy lies in my name, ch. 4. 10.

*{and the Priests bear rule by their means;}* Heb. *the Priests,* or *Princes,* (for the word will bear either: See on Esay 61. 10.) *rule upon,* or *at,* or *by, their hands:* as Esay 62. 3. This some render of the princes, whom, say they, the false prophets confirmed in their rapines, and robberies, being by them bribed so to do, Ezek. 13. 22. So some of the Jewish doctors. Other of them expound it, of the corrupt carriage of the princes in taking of bribes, Hos. 4. 18. Mic. 7. 3. and because the word here used, is found, Judg. 14. 9. where it is said of Samson, that *he took in his hands* of the honey that he found in the carcass of the lion; they would therefore have it here so to signify, the princes, or priests, *take* bribes, that are as sweet as honey to them, into their hands, to pervert the right, and to give wrong judgment. The ancient Greek, and the old Latin, following it, *The priests with their hands applaud them:* or, as a late writer would have the Greek to mean, *They applaud their,* that is, the false prophets', *hands;* as if they had read with other vowels, *they descend upon their hands.* But this the words, without some variation, will not admit. Most of ours, There is a combination between the priests, and the false prophets, and these, by their false prophecies, support and confirm the priests in their ambitious courses and corrupt carriages, whereby as Eli's sons sometime, 1 Sam. 2. 12, 17, 22. they domineered and tyrannized over God's people, and which the true prophets of God reproved in them. Nor does that swerve from this in effect and substance, which that learned late writer suggests, that the phrase *at the hand* here used, does usually signify *after,* or *according to,* the *leading, guidance,* or *direction* of some other: as Exod. 2. 5. Num. 13. 29. Josh. 15. 15. 2 Sam. 15. 18. (which place one of the Jewish commenters here points us to) 1 Chr. 25. 2, 3, 6. 2 Chr. 17. 14. & 31. 15. Neh. 3. 2, 4, 5. so it should be implied, that the priests ruled and swayed all, not so much by the ministry, as by the authority of the false prophets, who pretended an extraordinary call. Howsoever we take the term, certain it is, that they both banded together against God's prophets, ch. 26. 8. & 29. 25, 27.

*{and my people love to have it so:}* They like and love the lies and flatteries of the false prophets, better than God's truth, Esay 30. 10. Mic. 2. 6, 11. 2 Thess. 2. 9, 11.

*{and what will ye do in the end thereof?}* Some understand it, as spoken in the person of God, as rendering a reason of what he had said, v. 29. What will this wickedness grow unto, unless I do by some special penal course repress it? Others, rather, what will be the issue of this? what will become of you at last? when all sorts among you, prophets, priests, and people, are so extremely corrupt and faulty, what can be expected, but an utter riddance of you all? See ch. 6. 13. Mic. 3. 11.

## CHAPTER 6

**Verse 1.** *{O ye children of Benjamin gather yourselves}* The prophet proceeds to give warning of the Chaldeans' approach, vers. 1, 6. shows what misery and mischief should thereby befall them, vers. 21, 26. withal laying before them the causes of all this, to wit, the general corruption among all sorts with them, vers. 6, 7, 13, 28. and their willful obstinacy, in refusing to hearken to God's word, v. 8, 10, 17, 18. and to break off their wicked courses, vers. 29, 30.

*{O ye children of Benjamin,}* To the Benjaminites, the prophet directs his speech, as to forewarn them of the Babylonian expedition against Judah, and the siege of Jerusalem shortly after to ensue, because that tribe had adhered to Judah, when the other ten had revolted from it, 2 Chr. 11. 12. chap. 17. 26. and divers of that tribe did inhabit Jerusalem, part of the city lying within their lot, Joshua 18. 28.

*{gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem;}* Or, *retire;* as it was before rendered, chap. 4. 6. or *withdraw* yourselves. See on ch. 4. 6. *out of the midst of Jerusalem,* for, *out of Jerusalem:* as Num. 14. 44. As before they were advised to flee unto Jerusalem for succor and safeguard, as to a place of the greatest strength with them, ch. 4. 5, 6. thereby intimating the approach of the enemy unto their parts: so here on the other side, they are admonished to quit Jerusalem, and get speedily out of her, lest they be surprised in her, and perish together with her: and as afterward to leave the land of Judah, ch. 10. 17. thereby intimating her approaching siege, and what would become of her, whom they had repaired unto for shelter and safety. See the like Esay 23. 12. as that before rather foretelling what they would do, than seriously advising them so to do: so this telling them what indeed their best and wisest course would be: flee of Babylon, Esay 52. 11. ch. 51. 6.

*{and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in Beth-haccerem}* The blowing of the trumpet, and setting up of a sign, are to give people in those parts warning of the enemies' approach, and either thereby to incite them to make preparation for opposition, or to admonish them to betake themselves to places of strength; as ch. 4. 5, 6. Hos. 5. 8. & 8. 1. not that they should indeed be able to make head against so potent an enemy, or that in any place of strength they should find safety; but as foretelling what then would be done, and representing to them, what they would in those times be calling upon to have done, though it were to no purpose. See chap. 8. 14.

*{in Tekoa}* A city of Judah, 1 Chro. 2. 24. 2 Chro. 11. 6. Amos 1. 1. it was situate on an hill, and lay toward the north of Judah, which way the enemy was to come; and there is in the Hebrew an elegancy of like sound, in the name of *Tekoa,* and the term of *trumpeting:* the like whereunto is also found, Mic. 1. 10, 14. Zeph. 2. 4. so that it is as if he had said, do that which your name imports.

*{set up a sign of fire}* That is, *fire a beacon.* So some of the Rabbines here expound it, whom also not a few follow; supposing the verb whence it comes to have sometime a notion of *burning* in it, and so to be used, 2 Sam. 5. 21. Job 7. 13. & 22. 23. Nah. 1. 5. and this word to be in that sense derived from it, and so to signify, both here and elsewhere, Judg. 20. 38, 40. & Ezek. 17. 9. but there is not one of those places, but is very questionable, and may well therefore otherwise be rendered: and though it be true, that the firing of a beacon may well be comprehended among many other signs or significations, of the use intended in the term here used; yet is the word a term of a far larger extent, and it imports anything whatsoever thus set up for a sign, whether banner displayed, or beacon fired, or aught else of the like use: and the text is no more word for word, than *lift up a lift-up;* or some *signal,* so called, because erected or lift up: let somewhat be set up that may give notice to the parts adjacent of the enemies' approach: that which was called *an ensign,* or *a standard,* chap. 4. 6. but the term here used, is more general: and so Judg. 20. 28. *that they should cause to ascend a great lift-up* (if we may so speak) *of smoke:* and v. 40. *when the lift-up of smoke began to ascend:* not unlike to that Esa. 9. 18. though another term there be used, *to lift up a lift-up:* as, *to vow a vow,* Gen. 28. 20. *to fast a fast,* 2 Sam. 12. 16. *to serve a service,* Exo. 13. 5. *to judge a judgment,* ch. 5. 28. See also, v. 13.

*{in Beth-haccerem}* Heb. *on Beth-haccerem:* that is, *on the house of the vineyard.* So one of the Jewish commenters, expounding it *of a tower,* or *turret;* erected in a vineyard to oversee it, and the neighboring one, and for a watchman to watch in, for the preservation of them, Esa. 5. 2. and the manner of writing, in Hebrew, the two terms standing apart, with no such line intervenient, as our Version exhibits, might seem to add some strength hereunto: but the like is found in some other proper names, as Esay 8. 3. where though in our Version the like lines are inserted, yet in the Hebrew text, none such appear. The Chaldee Paraphrast renders it, *on the house of the valley of the vineyards:* Nor can I but wonder, why a writer of great note should say the word there used should signify cities situate on hills. But another of the Jewish doctors says, that it is the proper name of a place, and so the ancient Greek, and old Latin, take it; and, as some say, also, the Syrian: And Jerome reports, that Beth-haccerem was a town situate on an hill between Tekoa and Jerusalem, from whence Tecoa was not above twelve miles distant: It seems to be the same with *Beth-haccerem,* mentioned Nehemiah 3. 14. and of this stamp were the names of many cities in those parts: as *Bethaven,* Josh. 18. 1. *Bethana,* Josh. 19. 38. *Bethania,* John 11. 1. *Betharabah,* Josh. 15. 6. *Bethbarah,* Judg. 7. 24. or *Bethabarah,* Joh. 1. 28. *Bethlehem,* Josh. 19. 15. Matt. 2. 1. *Bethsaida,* Matth. 11. 21. *Bethesda,* Joh. 5. 2.

*{for evil appeareth out of the North,}* From the northern parts, by the Babylonians marching towards them from Chaldea, that lay north from them, ch. 1. 14. & 3. 18. & 4. 6.

*{and great destruction.}* Heb. *and* (or, *even,* as Esay 65. 6.) *a great* (or, *grievous) breach,* or, *breaking:* as chap. 4. 20. & 48. 3. So cha. 4. 6.

**Verse 2.** *{I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.}* These words are diversely taken, and diversely rendered. The word *woman,* is not in the text: but there is a defect of the subject; as, *standing,* for, *standing* corn: and, *fruitful,* for, *fruitful* vine, Esay 17. 5, 6. And some supply *woman,* as our Version does: but about the former attribute, the Jewish doctors are divided; for some of them say, that it signifies a woman that *inhabiteth;* one that dwells, or keeps at home, not out of an housewifely care, as Titus 2. 5. but out of delicacy and nicety, a loathness to look out, or set her foot on the ground, as Deu. 28. 56. as coming from a word that signifies *to inhabit,* or *to keep at home:* as it is rendered, Hab. 2. 5. Others of them expound it, *a comely,* or *beautiful* woman; as the Rabbines frequently use the word whence it comes: and as another, whereof anon, very near it, is used, and rendered, Cant. 1. 10. Prov. 17. 7. & 19. 10. & 26. 1. and some of ours, which admitting this supply, will the better suit with what ensues, would have some fair shepherdess intended, whose love many shepherds seeking to obtain, come and pitch their tents, and feed their flocks near to her. But there want not those, who supply not *woman,* but *land;* and read the words; *I have likened the daughter of Zion to a goodly pasture* ground, and, *a delicate* land: such as Asher is said to be, affording *royal dainties,* Gen. 49. 20. and indeed the former word differs in gender only from the term that does usually signify *a pasture;* as it is well rendered, Ezek. 34. 14. though in some other places elsewhere, amiss: as also the same word is rendered *a pleasant place,* Hosea 9. 13. whence also some of the Jewish critics expound it, both here, and elsewhere, as by intercision of a letter not unusual, derived from a root that signifies *to desire,* and as the same with *desired,* or *desirable,* such as good and beautiful things usually are, (whence also the words in the places before pointed to) and such pasture grounds to shepherds; in regard whereof also, is *Naioth* deemed to have its name, 1 Sam. 19. 19. And to this the rather I incline; because both the word may well bear it, and it suits exceeding well with the ensuing expressions, vers. 3. So that it is as if the prophet had said, Methinks Jerusalem (for that is the daughter of Zion, Esay 1. 8.) seems very like (as the former) to some beautiful and delicate dame, living plentifully and daintily in her own land, as at home; or, according to the latter, to some goodly pleasant pasture land, that may well entice shepherds to repair to it with their flocks. One difference more there is among the Jewish critics, about the verb here used, which some of them understand as we have it here rendered; and so it is taken, Cant. 1. 9. Howbeit, because the word is there in another form: and in the form here used, it signifies generally, this one place excepted, wheresoever it is found in a notion of similitude, not *to liken,* but *to be like,* as Psal. 144. 4. Cant. 7. 7. Ezek. 31. 8. Some of them therefore would have it here expounded, not, *I have likened,* but, *I have cut off,* or, *I will cut off:* as the very same word is in this form used, Hos. 4. 5. where it is rendered, *I will destroy thy mother.* According to this interpretation it should be read without any supply, *The fair and delicate daughter of Zion have I destroyed,* or, *will I destroy;* for so the words lie in the text: but the attributes are not wont in Hebrew thus in construction to lead their subject: and for the verb, both in this, and some other, the forms are sometime confounded.

**Verse 3.** *{The Shepherds with their flocks shall come unto her;}* That is, the Babylonian princes and chieftains with their forces, as shepherds invited by her pleasant pastures fit for their flocks: So ch. 12. 10. and there seems a secret taunt in the term of *shepherds;* as the like in *watchers,* and *keepers,* ch. 4. 16, 17.

*{with their flocks}* Heb. *and their flocks;* as ch. 1. 13.

*{they shall pitch their tents against her round about,}* *Pitch tents;* as shepherds do, Esa. 13. 20. the warlike *tents* here intended, as ch. 37. 10. a defect of the pronoun; as Esa. 13. 22.

*{against her round about}* As ch. 4. 16, 17. or, *besides her;* as the particle is used, Esa. 32. 20. they shall lie in siege about her, ch. 1. 15. & 4. 17. Ezek. 4. 2, 3.

*{they shall feed every one in his place}* Heb. *a man* (for, each one, as ch. 5. 8.) *his hand;* which the Greek renders, *with his hand:* they shall by might and force, as we use to say, *with strong hand,* destroy and spoil. So, *with the hand,* Esay 28. 2. The old Latin, those that be *under his hand:* *his companies;* So the Chaldee; as, *the sheep of his hand,* Psal. 95. 7. Others, *at his side:* beside him; what is next to him: as, *the asses* were *feeding at the hand* [word obscured] *them;* that is, *beside them,* Job 1. 14. Others, *they shall feed each one his place,* or, *they shall depasture,* or, *eat down,* (destroy and devour, as beasts are wont to depasture a ground. See Esa. 3. 14.) *his place,* or, *his* [word obscured] assigned him. So is the word *hand,* used, [reference obscured] 2. 17. Deut. 23. 12. [reference obscured] 5, 11. & 57. 8. they shall take up their quarters, and acco[letters obscured]ing to their employments in such and such places assigned them, they shall spoil and make havoc of all that they can. And this last I conceive to be the genuine notion and use of the word in this place.

**Verse 4.** *{Prepare ye war against her}* Heb. *Sanctify:* as chap. 12. 3. & 22. 7. Joel 3. 9. So Esay 13. 3. *I have commanded my sanctified ones.* The words of God himself; and, as I take it, of no other here: though most interpreters understand them, as the words of the Babylonian king, or the Chaldean princes, giving order for preparation; and suppose it to have reference to some solemn rites that the heathen used, in denouncing war; and some also to the fire, that the Chaldeans, say they, made an idol of, and had borne before them in their camp. See on chap. 1. 13. But neither of these conceits seem to be very probable, as to the word here used; the use of it in this kind being so large, and so indefinite. But for the party, in whose person this is spoken, whosoever he or they be, the prophet here gives over his former resemblance; and that they may understand more clearly, what manner of *Shepherds* they were, that were coming against them, he tells them here, that they were warriors, military men, unto whom God had given a charge and commission against them. See Esa. 10. 5, 6. v. 6.

*{Arise, and let us go up at noon.}* These words, without question, hold out the speeches of those, whom God in his secret counsel had designed unto that service, and by an efficacious instinct stirred up thereunto; encouraging and inciting one another, with all speed, to set upon it, and with all eagerness to pursue it: the prophet thereby intimating, as I conceive, how ready they should be to put in execution, what God would have done by them, so soon as ever the time was come, wherein God would have it effected. See Esay 5. 26, 27.

*{Arise}* As chap. 1. 17. So Deut. 2. 13. Esay 21. 5. chap. 49. 14.

*{let us go up}* Let us march; a military term. See Isaiah 7. 1.

*{at noon}* Which some expound, as an argument of courage, as who should say; we shall not need to steal in upon them by night, we will set upon them at noonday, 1 King. 20. 16. chap. 15. 8. Zeph. 2. 4. Others, as an intimation of their present strength and flourishing estate, in regard whereof, they needed not to misdoubt aught, but were sure to carry all before them with success at pleasure; *day light,* for, *prosperity;* as Esther 8. 16. Esay 59. 9. But these seem to be both wide of the prophet's intendment. Nor comes the Jewish doctor anything nearer, who tells us, that *noon,* and *night,* here mentioned the one, and in the next verse the other, are times of unlucky occurrents, according to that, Psal. 91. 6. But they seem rather the words of men, manifesting an impatiency of delay, and calling one upon another, either to march on, and set forward, so soon as they are got together, though it be at noonday; or to assault the city instantly, though it be noonday, ere they can come to sit down before it; albeit that the heat of the day at noontide, in those hot countries especially, be nothing commodious or seasonable, either for march, or assault: and complaining, that by delay and stay, they do but burn daylight. And to this purpose, one of the Jewish commenters understanding this whole passage, not of their march towards Jerusalem, but of the city, accordingly expounds and applies the several terms here used; *Prepare war;* make ready to give an assault: *arise,* out of your several quarters, v. 3. *go up;* scale the walls: as v. 5, 10. that we may surprise the city, ere night approach: and as vexed that they cannot take it and sack it the same day. But I conceive it rather to be meant of their march; and their forward desire to be making on towards it.

*{woe unto us; for the day goeth away, and the shadows of the evening are stretched out.}* This the Jewish commenters, and many other treading in their steps, understand as the voice of God's people, or the prophet speaking in their person, lamenting their woeful condition, and complaining, that all their prosperity was drawing to a period, and the night of affliction was ready to surprise them; according to that, Amos 8. 9, 10. But others rather conceive it to be a continuation of the voices of the Chaldeans, and their complices, eagerly desirous to be setting on forward, and complaining that the day spent, and they lost so much time, while by needless delays, they retarded their expedition, and let slip their opportunities; as chap. 46. 17.

*{for the day goeth away}* Or, *that* (as chap. 4. 18. Lam. 5. 16.) *the day passeth away;* or, *spendeth;* as Psal. 90. 9. a metaphor from one that at parting, turns his face from us. See on Isay 53. 6. chap. 2. 27.

*{the shadows of the evening are stretched out}* Or, *are lengthened;* as towards evening they use to be: *I decline,* as Psal. 102. 11. & 109. 23.

**Verse 5.** *{Arise, and let us go up by night}* Let us march night and day, that we may lose no time. See vers. 4.

*{and let us destroy her palaces.}* Or, *that we may destroy her palaces:* as chap. 5. 28. that which made them so eager upon this expedition, to have the spoil of the city, the king's house, and the state-houses of his princes, and great men, stored with much wealth, and costly house furniture. See Esay 13. 22. and 32. 14. & 30. 6. chap. 22. 1.

**Verse 6.** *{For thus hath the LORD of hosts said;}* Or, *Thus saith the Lord of hosts:* as chap. 5. 14. That you may not think that these men come led on only by their own ambitious, or covetous affections and dispositions; be it known unto you, that God has an hand in the business; it is he that sets them on work, to execute his wrath upon you for your sins and excesses, chap. 1. 15, 16. See vers. 4.

*{Hew ye down trees}* To raise works for the siege, and make engines for a battery, such as were then in use, Deut. 20. 19, 20.

*{cast a mount}* Or, *discharge engines of shot.* See on Isa. 37. 33. So Ezek. 26. 8.

*{this is the city to be visited}* Or, *punished;* as chap. 5. 9, 29. the time of her visitation by judgment is come, chap. 11. 23. & 23. 12. Ezek. 9. 1. Hos. 9. 7. the time of God's wrathful visitation of them, because of his gracious visitation neglected by them, Luk. 19. 44. their sins being risen (as the next words imply) to the height, Ezek. 7. 10, 12. 1 Thess. 2. 16.

*{she is wholly oppression in the midst of her.}* There is nothing but oppression in her. She is so full of it from the one end to the other, as if she were all made of it, 2 Kin. 21. 16. & 24. 4. Ezek. 7. 23. See of Nineveh, Nah. 3. 1.

*{in the midst of her.}* As Psal. 55. 11.

**Verse 7.** *{As a fountain casteth out her waters, so she casteth out her wickedness.}* These abuses flow incessantly from her, as water from a spring; they are renewed daily with her; they never depart from her: she is in regard of them, as a spring that is never drawn dry, Psal. 55. 9, 11.

*{casteth out}* Or, *causeth to spring up,* or, *issue out:* whence a word signifying *a well,* or, *spring,* ch. 2. 13. properly one discovered and procured by *digging;* for the verb in its first notion signifies *to dig,* 2 Kin. 19. 24. Isa. 37. 25.

*{her wickedness}* As the working sea does *mire* and *dirt.* Isaiah 57. 20.

*{violence and spoil is heard in her;}* That is the common cry with her; it is that all the city rings of. See ch. 20. 8.

*{before me continually is grief and wounds}* Heb. *disease and stroke,* or, *stripe:* as Deut. 28. 61. their cruel courses in vexing and oppressing one another, and the cry thereby caused, are continually in mine ear the one, in mine eye the other; provoking and urging me to proceed in all severity and rigor against her. See Exod. 22. 22–27. Psa. 109. 15. Isa. 3. 8, 14, 15. & 59. 13, 18. & 65. 3. Luke 12. 28. Jam. 5. 4. Howbeit, some expound all this, not of evils committed by them, but of evils to be inflicted upon them; which the prophet should have continually in his ear, and his eye; as the *standard,* and *trumpet* leading on, and inciting to them, ch. 4. 21. but the former more easily flows from the text.

**Verse 8.** *{Be thou instructed, O Jerusalem}* A summons of them to repentance. Heb. *Be corrected.* Take warning, and be amended by the judgments, that already have befallen you: for the word signifies in the first place, *to chastise,* ch. 31. 18. Hos. 10. 10. and in the next place, *by chastising, to reform and amend,* Prov. 29. 15. See ch. 2. 30. & 5. 3.

*{lest my soul depart from thee,}* Heb. *be loosed,* or, *disjointed from me:* a metaphor taken from the dislocation of a limb, the forcing of it from its natural place and posture, and putting it, as we say, out of joint, Gen. 32. 25. intimating what a pain and grief it is to God to leave, or cast off a people, whom he is once in league with, and with how much difficulty he is drawn thereunto. So Ezek. 23. 17, 18. *soul,* for, the person himself: as ch. 5. 9, 29. but here somewhat more specially *for love* and *affection,* whereof the soul is the seat: as Gen. 34. 8. Psa. 42. 1, 2. Lev. 26. 11, 15, 30.

*{lest I make thee desolate, a land not inhabited.}* Heb. *lest I make thee a desolation,* or, *a waste,* as chap. 4. 27, 29. I will both cast you off, and cut you off, two grand evils, dereliction, and destruction: and the one of them usually following on the other. Hence that, *Woe to them, when I depart from them,* Hos. 10. 12.

**Verse 9.** *{Thus saith the LORD of hosts}* As before, v. 6.

*{They shall thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel as a vine:}* *They* (the enemy, the Chaldeans, compared to *grape-gatherers;* as chap. 49. 9.) Heb. *shall gleaning glean;* that is, thoroughly glean; an allusion to the law, that inhibited the going over the vine again, after the general cutting, or the leaving of it wholly bare, Lev. 19. 10. Deut. 24. 21. the meaning is, that the enemy in cutting them off, or captiving them, should go over them again and again: as it is said of the Israelites, when they had discomfited the main body of the Benjaminites, they afterward *gleaned* them, as they lighted on them straggling in the highways, Judg. 20. 45. and thus did the Chaldeans *glean the remnant of Israel,* the people of Judah; not so called in regard of the ten tribes, before by the Assyrian destroyed, 2 Kin. 17. 6. but in regard of those of their own people, and their city, whom, and which, the Chaldeans had before plundered, captived, or cut off, not in the time of Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin only, 2 Kin. 24. 2, 13, 16. but in Zedekiah's reign, when at several times, they spoiled, killed, and carried away of them, 2 Kin. 25. 4. See Esa. 6. 13. ch. 10. 16. & 52. 3, 30. Of the name *Israel,* see ch. 5. 15, 20.

*{as a vine}* For the word here used, is peculiar to the vine, Judg. 8. 2. Esa. 24. 14. of *gleanings* of corn, another word is used, Lev. 19. 9. Ruth 2. 2, 3.

*{turn back thine hand as a grape-gatherer into the baskets.}* Heb. *upon the baskets.* God speaks, say some, to Jeremy, bidding him pull off the clusters of grapes, from a vine in vision represented unto him, one after another, until he had plucked all, and bestowed them in a basket. Others, to the Chaldeans enjoining them to spoil, and kill, and carry away again and again, until they had made a clean riddance of them. The Jewish doctors conceive them to be the words of the Chaldeans, inciting one another to spoil and plunder, and massacre, or captive again and again, while any persons of regard, or matter worth the carrying away, remained; to which purpose also, some here insert the word *saying;* as chap. 4. 31. See vers. 4. I concur with the middle, and conceive a great spoil, and that redoubled, both of persons and prey to be intimated; though not an utter extirpation of either. See Esa. 6. 13. cha. 5. 10. & 52. 16. 2 Kin. 25. 12, 22.

**Verse 10.** *{To whom shall I speak and give warning, that they may hear?}* The prophet's complaint of an unteachable, and untractable disposition, that did generally possess this people. See the like, Isa. 28. 9.

*{To whom}* As Esa. 53. 1.

*{give warning}* Heb. *protest;* as ch. 11. 7.

*{that they may hear}* To take warning and obey: as ch. 7. 23, 24. Heb. *and they will hear:* as v. 5. Josh. 24. 9. Mal. 1. 9.

*{behold their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken.}* Or, *that they cannot hearken;* as before: That is, say some, they have a mere carnal and fleshly ear, that apprehends not, nor admits aught that is spiritual, 1 Cor. 2. 14. Col. 2. 13. Others, their minds and hearts are so possessed with sensuality, security, and willful obstinacy, that they regard not aught that is delivered to them from God, though it never so nearly concern them, and their own welfare and good. See Luke 8. 14. & 21. 34. It has reference, say some, to such as have ears stopped with *earwax,* and such like foisty stuff that hinders their hearing; but rather to the *foreskin,* that in circumcision was taken away, (see chap. 4. 4.) and to such persons, as having a thick skin or film, growing over the organ of hearing, are thereby deprived of the use of that sense, implying, that they no more regarded any of God's messages, than as if it were so with them, as with such it is. So Act. 7. 51. See Psal. 58. 4, 5. vers. 16. ch. 7. 26. Zech. 7. 11. Act. 7. 57.

*{the word of the LORD is unto them a reproach}* They account it as matter, not of reproof, but of reproach; such as men cannot endure to hear. So rather, than as some, they make it matter of reproach to those that deliver it, chap. 20. 8.

*{they have no delight in it}* They cannot brook it, they have no love nor liking at all to it. See chap. 5. 31. 2 Thess. 2. 10, 12. 2 Tim. 4. 3.

**Verse 11.** *{Therefore I am full of the fury of the LORD, I am weary with holding in: I will pour it forth upon the children abroad, and upon the assembly of young men together: for even the husband with the wife shall be taken, the aged with him that is full of days.}* The prophet, in these words, professes that, though he be most unwilling to denounce so dreadful and hideous a doom as God has passed upon his people, such as all sorts, without respect of age, or sex, were to suffer in, yet the spirit of prophecy is so full in him, and powerful upon him, that he is no longer able to keep it in, but he must of necessity denounce it. See the like profession, though upon another occasion, ch. 20. 9.

*{Therefore}* As ch. 1. 17. & 3. 3. Heb. *and;* which I see not why it should not here be retained: for it is not so much, as I conceive, the consideration of aught with them, as the Spirit of prophecy within him, that enforces him to this work.

*{full of the fury}* Or, *wrath.* Heb. *fervor,* or *heat:* that fire of God's wrath, whereof ch. 4. 4. & 5. 14. See ch. 15. 17.

*{I am weary with holding in:}* *Holding it in:* as ch. 4. 4. forbearing to denounce it, like Elihu, Job 32. 18, 20. So ch. 20. 9.

*{I will pour it forth}* The prophets are said to do what they denounce to be done. So ch. 1. 10. & 15. 1.

*{pour}* A borrowed speech taken from shouts of rain, that the heavens pour down, Psa. 11. 6. Isa. 24. 18. ch. 7. 20. & 10. 25. Ezek. 14. 18. & 22. 22. Rev. 16. 1.

*{pour it forth}* A defect of the pronoun, as before. Heb. *in pouring out,* I will pour out; that is, I will surely, or without more ado, without further delay, pour it out: a defective form of speech: the like whereunto, see Isa. 59. 13. ch. 14. 5.

*{upon the children abroad}* Or, *in the streets;* as the Chaldee renders it: and the word is used, 1 King. 20. 35. whither children use to run out, and where they use to play together, Zech. 8. 5. chap. 9. 21. intimating the Chaldeans should show no mercy to any, not so much as to young children, 2 Chr. 36:17. Ps. 127:8, 9. verse 21. Hos. 10:14.

*{upon the assembly of young men together}* The word here used signifies first a secret, Ps. 25:14. Prov. 11:13. then a secret place, Ps. 31:20. then a secret meeting, a conventicle, ch. 15:17: and lastly, any assembly, as well public, as private, Ps. 89:7. so here, upon the place where the young men meet to make merry together, ch. 31:13. though it may probably be deemed to have a privy glance at their common meetings in bad houses for evil purposes, ch. 5:7.

*{for even the husband with the wife shall be taken}* Or, *that the husband also with the wife may be taken*: as the particle is used, Job 6:11. ch. 4:13. or, *surely the husband also with the wife shall be taken*: so is the particle rendered, Isa. 49:18. & 60:9. or, as the Hebrew has it, *man with woman*, that is, *man and woman*; as v. 12. the one sex with the other: no regard being had more to the one than to the other. See Isa. 3:16, 24. & 32:9, 10. *shall be taken*, that is, surprised, and so fall into the cruel enemies' hands; as ch. 8:9. Lam. 4:20. and so is the word to be taken, Luke 17:34, 36. though interpreters go most there a contrary way.

*{the aged with him that is full of days}* Heb. *the old with the full of days*, with the decrepit; with him that has the one foot already in the grave. Of the phrase, see Isa. 65:20. such as were, in the course of nature, at the pit's brink; such as, though they should have spared them, yet could not have lived long; as he of Jeremy, in regard of the famine in the city, ch. 38:9. of the Chaldeans' cruelty towards the aged, see 2 Chr. 36:17. Isa. 47:6. Lam. 5:12, 13.

**Verse 12.** *{And their houses shall be turned unto others, with their fields, and wives, together.}* A defect of the pronoun in the latter branch, but supplied from the former; as Isa. 49:22, 23. Heb. *and women*; which may be of larger extent than *wives* only, and may comprehend both concubines, and maidservants also, as well as wives. The meaning is, that all should fall into the enemies' hands. See this threatened long before, Deut. 28:30. and again, ch. 8:10.

*{to others}* That is, *to aliens*, or *strangers*, as Prov. 5:9.

*{wives}* Heb. *women*; as ch. 7:18. & 8:10.

*{for I will stretch out my hand upon the inhabitants of the land, saith the LORD.}* See Isa. 5:25.

*{upon}* Or, *against*; as ch. 15:6.

*{the land}* Or, *this land*; as ch. 5:30.

**Verse 13.** *{For}* Or, *Because*; as ch. 3:25. A reason rendered of this severe denunciation: the generality of corruption among them, and among those especially who should have reproved and restrained it in others, and given example of better things. See v. 6.

*{from the least of them, even unto the greatest of them, every one is given to covetousness:}* Heb. *from the little of them, and unto the great of them*: a proverbial form of speech used frequently in Scripture, to express the generality of any practice, good or bad, among persons of all sorts and ranks, 2 Chr. 34:30. Est. 1:5, 20. ch. 31:34. & 42:8. *little*, for, *least*; and, *great*, for, *greatest*; as Est. 1:5, 20. Jon. 3:5. so, *good*, for, *best*; and *upright*, for, *uprightest*, Mic. 7:4. for nouns, in Hebrew, have no forms of comparison; and in such collations therefore, they make use of the positive, Ps. 118:8, 9. Prov. 22:1. Eccl. 7:1.

*{every one is given to covetousness}* Heb. *is coveting covetise*; as Prov. 1:19. & 15:7. Hab. 2:9. See the same charge, ch. 8:10. and the like phrase, v. 1.

*{and from the prophet, even to the priest, every one dealeth falsely}* Heb. *from prophet and to priest* (as before; that is, *both the priests and the prophets*; as, *from man, and unto beast*, for, *both man and beast*, Exod. 9:25. ch. 50:3.) *each one is doing falsehood*, as if that were their common trade: so Prov. 10:4. & 11:18. See also the same manner of expression, Matt. 24:38, 39. *to do falsehood*, for, *to deal falsely*; as, *not to do truth*, for, *not to deal truly*, 1 John 1:6. See also, ch. 8:10. As *covetousness* is charged upon the princes and people; so *falsehood*, or false dealing upon the priests and prophets: not that these were free from the former vice, (see Isa. 56:11. ch. 5:31.) or those from the latter (for of such distributive forms of speech, see on Isa. 5:13.) But this was the more special corruption reigning among the false prophets and the priests; that by their false prophecies and flatteries, they deceived the people, and soothed them up in their sins. See ch. 4:10. verse 14.

**Verse 14.** *{They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace, when there is no peace?}* They do by their glossings and flatteries lull people asleep in security, bearing them in hand, that there is no such dangerous matter towards them, as God's prophets tell them, but that all shall be well, whatsoever they say. See the same, ch. 8:11. See also, Lam. 2:14. Ezek. 13:22.

*{They have healed also}* Or, *They heal also*. Heb. *And they heal*, which may well be retained; for it is an instance, and a pregnant one, of the deceitful dealing charged upon them, v. 13.

*{the hurt}* Heb. *bruise*, or *breach*; as ch. 4:20. & 10:19.

*{of the daughter of my people}* See ch. 4:11. So ch. 9:1.

*{slightly}* Heb. *upon a slight, or slighted thing*: which some interpret *slighting, or making nothing of it*: so the Greek. Others, *with some slight medicine*: so is the particle used, Ps. 92:4. *with words of falsehood*, says the Chaldee; with saying, *peace, peace*, which was a very light matter for them to say, so the Jewish commenters: and it was indeed an easy thing to say so, as they said it; though not as our Savior said the like, Matt. 9:4, 5. Others, *according to some slight thing*, or *according to the cure of some slight hurt*; supplying *cure* from the word *heal*; *hurt* from the word *bruise*, or *breach*, in the foregoing branch. Whether way we take it, the sense is plain, that the prophets and priests, dealt with the people and the state, as unfaithful physicians, or surgeons, with a fond and foolish patient, unwilling to apprehend how it is indeed with him; who, albeit his disease and wound be dangerous and deadly, yet make light of it, as if it were some slight matter, that might easily be helped, apply only some lenitive, or stupefying plasters unto it, that may for a time give ease, or take away the sense of pain for the present, and bear him in hand, that he shall do well enough with it, he need not fear or misdoubt ought; or that use lenitives only, where the disease requires caustics and corrosives, and draw a skin over places full of corrupt matter, that may cause them to fester the more inwardly, unto the patient's greater and further evil. See ch. 23:14. Lam. 2:14. Ezek. 13:10. Howbeit, because the word here used, has sometime a notion of *vilifying* and contempt, 1 Sam. 2:30. Hence the old Latin renders it, one while, *with contumely*, and *unto contumely*, another while: that which some expound; the former, unto the contempt and reproach of the true prophets; whom thereby they brought into disgrace with the people, 1 Kings 22:24. ch. 28:2, 4, 10, 11. the latter, unto such contempt and reproach, as by their means should befall the people, while being deluded by them, and giving credit to them, they neglect those courses, whereby their peace with God might have been procured, and those evils prevented that God's prophets gave them warning of. See to this purpose also, Lam. 2:14. But the words will not so easily admit this sense.

*{saying, peace, peace,}* A proverbial form of speech, implying as much as that which we use to say, *all shall be well*: so, *is it peace?* for, *is all well?* 2 Kings 4:26. & 9:17, 18. and, *it shall be peace*; for, *all shall be well*, 2 Kings 4:23.

*{and there is no peace}* Or, *when there is no peace*; when as meanwhile there is no such matter, there is nothing well, but all full of deadly danger, ch. 4:10. Heb. *and*, (for, *when*; as Isa. 3:3. & 37:9, 36.) *peace is not*, as 2 Chr. 15:5. Isa. 57:21. so Ezek. 13:10.

**Verse 15.** *{Were they at all ashamed, when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not ashamed, neither could they blush.}* Their sin is further aggravated by their shamelessness in it, as ch. 3:3. some read the words, *Did they make them ashamed?* as if the meaning were, did they labor to bring the people to a sight of their abominable courses, and to work them to shame and sorrow for them? and so the word indeed, in this form and notion is used, 2 Sam. 19:6. but not, that I find elsewhere; in this prophet constantly the former way, ch. 10:14. & 46:24. & 48:1, 20. & 50:2. & 51:17. So here, the Chaldee, Greek, and Latin take it, and the words following confirm it. See the same passage again, ch. 8:12.

*{when they had committed abomination}* That is, idolatry, say some, referring it to the people; but as I conceive rather such abominable things, as God saw, and complains of in the prophets, ch. 5:30, 31. & 23:14.

*{not at all ashamed}* Heb. *in being ashamed, ashamed*: or, *in being abashed, abashed*, which comes nearer to our English; of which manner of gemination, see Isa. 24:16. ch. 3:1.

*{neither could they blush}* Heb. *they know not to blush*; as Isa. 29:12. *I know not to read*, for, *I cannot read*: *they know not satiety*; for, *they cannot be satisfied*, Isa. 56:11. and Zeph. 3:5. *the wicked have not shame*: for though the latter word here used, be scarce found elsewhere, save in the transitive sense; that which seems to have given occasion of that diverse version; yet the former word, in this latter branch, is never so used, and that this latter is not to be so here taken, appears by the place parallel to this, ch. 8:12. where it is exhibited in a passive form, that admits no such ambiguity; and indeed, none were more shameless than their false prophets.

*{therefore shall they fall, among them that fall.}* That is, *be slain, among those that be slain*; and to whom they now promise safety; *to fall*; or, *to be slain*, as Ps. 63:10. Luke 21:24.

*{at the time that I visit them, they shall be cast down, saith the LORD}* Heb. *in the time, wherein I visit them*, (See v. 6. a defect of the relative, as ch. 5:17, 24.) *they shall by stumbling be made to fall*, or, *be thrown down*; as if they had stumbled, and fallen flat to the ground: for that is the word's native and proper notion, Ps. 27:2. Isa. 31:3. ch. 50:32. Dan. 11:19.

**Verse 16.** *{Thus saith the LORD, Stand ye in the ways and see and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein; and ye shall find rest for your souls.}* God proceeds here by the prophet, to convince this people of their obstinacy; and turns his speech now from the false prophets that seduced them, unto those that were seduced by them: relating both what advice he had from time to time given them, and how they had still refused to hearken thereunto. And in this verse, he seems to meet with an objection that the people might make; alleging for themselves, that they went that way, that their priests and prophets directed them unto, and led them in: to which the Lord answers, that he had from to time admonished them to do as travelers are wont to do, when they are at a loss, or in some doubt of their way; seeing divers ways or paths before them, and know not which of them leads unto the place that they are bound for, they are careful to make inquiry of such as are able aright to inform them, which is the way that leads to such a place: and so should they do, if they made doubt of the way they were in, or of those divers ways, that they were invited unto by those prophets, that spoke unto them in the name of the Lord; as both the true prophets of God, and the false prophets also did; they should make a stand, and enter into a due consideration concerning either, whether of them were the way, that might conduce to their good, and welfare; and to help and further themselves in this inquiry, should have recourse to God's oracles, and the sacred records of the former ages, and times therein registered; and consider what way it was, that is therein commended to them, and has ever proved successful and advantageous to those that walked in it; and that betaking themselves unto that, and walking in it, whatsoever any might suggest, or inform them to the contrary, they should be sure to do well, as those before them had done, so Deut. 32:7. Isa. 8:20. Mal. 4:4. Luke 16:29. 1 Thess. 5:21. 1 John 4:1. And this I take to be the genuine, both drift and sense of this place.

*{stand in the ways}* Or, *on the ways*: as travelers, when at a stand, uncertain which way to take, Ezek. 21:19, 22.

*{and see}* Or, *consider*: as ch. 2:19.

*{ask for the old paths}* *Inquire after them*: after those that God by Moses prescribed you, say some; after those that your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and other godly after them walked in, say others; or, *inquire concerning them*: as the particle is used, Isa. 56:4. ch. 14:10. Heb. *concerning the paths of antiquity*; as, *the days of antiquity*, Deut. 32:7. that is, the times that men of former ages lived in, and the courses that men of former ages took and walked in.

*{where is the good way}* Or, *which of them is the good way*, or, *the best way*: *good*, for, *best*; as, *great*, for, *greatest*; *little*, for, *least*, v. 13. for other degrees of comparison, the Hebrew have not. Heb. *where the good way is*: the pronoun demonstrative, for the verb substantive; as Ps. 25:12. Isa. 66:1. They much mistake the text who hence would prove, that the old way is the best way; to which purpose, many both Papists and Protestants abuse it: for the prophet does not say, nor God by the prophet, that the oldest way is the best, but wills them to inquire, which of those of former ages proved the best unto those that walked in it: so Moses, Deut. 4:3, 4. and Deborah, Judg. 5:6, 8. and Azariah, 2 Chr. 15:2, 6. and this our prophet, ch. 22:15, 17.

*{and walk therein}* Take to, and keep to that way, that upon due inquiry you find to have been such, 1 Thess. 5:21.

*{and ye shall find rest to your souls}* That is, say some, your minds shall then be settled, you shall not hang in suspense, wavering between two ways; as those in Elijah's time, 1 Kings 18:21. or, rather, you shall find freedom from that restless condition, you now remain in, Isa. 57:20. from those fears and distractions, and such evils and troubles, as by the courses you now take, you procure to yourselves, having assurance of protection and safety from God. See Deut. 33:12, 29. Ps. 95:11. Isa. 28:12. Matt. 11:29. *your souls*, for, *yourselves*; as Isa. 55:2, 3.

*{but they said, we will not walk therein}* Albeit, they had it by my prophets so evidently showed them, that the way which they directed them unto, and called upon them to take, was the only good, and safe, and advantageous way, and had from time to time so proved unto those that walked constantly in it, that they could not but be clearly in conscience convinced of it; yet out of a self-willed obstinacy, they refuse to turn to it, and walk in it. See ch. 2:25. & 18:11, 12. Heb. *And they said*; *and*, for, *but*; as ch. 5:3. or, as some read the place, inserting the words, *when I say* (as Ps. 27:8.) *stand on the ways, and see or inquire which way of former times was the best, and walk therein; they say, We will not walk in it.* See the like syntax, ch. 2:25. Isa. 30:20. & 35:4.

*{walk therein}* Or, *in it*: supplied, as Deut. 8:12. Isa. 35:9.

**Verse 17.** *{Also I set watchmen over you, saying, Hearken to the sound of the trumpet; but they said, We will not hearken.}* Or, as some render it, *Again*, he says, *I have set watchmen over you. hearken ye therefore to the sound of the trumpet; but they said, We will not hearken.* Or, *And when I set watchmen over you, saying, Hearken to the sound of the trumpet; they say, We will not hearken*; as before, v. 16. So Isa. 37:9, 36. & 44:4. & 53:2.

*{watchmen}* God's ministers and messengers, set over them, to watch for their welfare, and to warn them of approaching evils, that they may be prevented. See ch. 1:10. v. 27. Isa. 56:10. Ezek. 3:17. & 33:7. Heb. 13:17.

*{over you}* Or, *over them*, because *they* follows: as Job 18:4. ch. 2:6, 7. & 7:26.

*{saying}* Inserted; as Ps. 105:15. Job 8:18. Acts 7:32.

*{hearken to the sound of the trumpet}* The voice of God's ministers, Isa. 58:1. giving warning of approaching evils, Ezek. 33:2, 6. an allusion to the blowing of the trumpet, mentioned ch. 4:5. v. 1.

*{they said}* Or, *they say*; as v. 16. a passage from person to person: as Isa. 1:29. ch. 5:19.

*{we will not hearken}* To it; as, *walk in it*, v. 16. See the like peremptory answers, ch. 22:21. & 44:16.

**Verse 18.** *{Therefore hear ye, O nations; and know, O congregation, what is among them.}* In these words, and the next ensuing, God being about further to lay forth this people's perverse, and pertinacious carriages, together with the penalties that for the same should deservedly befall them, takes all the world to witness, even the senseless creatures themselves among the rest, of the obstinacy of his people, and the equity of his dealing with them; turning his speech unto others, because they would not hear him. See the like, Isa. 1:2.

*{hear ye nations}* That you may not wonder, that I should proceed in this manner with that people, whom I had formerly taken into my protection, and by solemn covenant and promises so engaged myself unto. See Lam. 4:12.

*{know}* Or, *take notice*: as ch. 2:19. & 3:13. Isa. 33:13.

*{O congregation}* Of Israel, say some: of any foreign people, as others rather: as Ps. 7:7.

*{what is among them}* Or, *how it is with them*; what a height of disobedience and rebellion they are grown to, that you may understand how just cause I have to proceed thus against them; though some render it, as of the evils to be inflicted upon them, *what shall befall them*: but the words better admit the former.

**Verse 19.** *{Hear, O earth}* That which this people will not hear. So Isa. 1:2. ch. 22:19. for I suppose they are wide, who by *the earth*, here, understand *mankind*: as Ps. 98:9.

*{behold, I will bring evil upon this people, even the fruit of their thoughts}* Or, *Behold*, (be you as certainly assured of it, as if you saw it already done: as Isa. 7:14. & 65:27.) *I am bringing evil upon this people*, (as ch. 11:11. & 19:3. See ch. 4:6.) *even* (Heb. *and*; as v. 1.) *the fruit of their thoughts*, or, *counsels*, or, *contrivements*. See Isa. 55:7. & 59:7. ch. 4:14. *the fruit* of them, that, say some, that shall be proportionable to them, Ps. 28:4. or that rather, which by those courses and contrivances, they have procured to themselves, Prov. 1:31. for that seems too nice, which one of the Jewish doctors suggests; that he says not *their works*, but, *their thoughts*: those, to wit, by which they thought, that God saw not their works, Ps. 94:7. Isa. 29:15.

*{because they have not hearkened unto my words,}* Heb. *upon*, for, *unto*; as verse 10. unto my messages brought to them by my prophets, and advices by them from me given them, verses 16, 17. Prov. 1:24, 25.

*{nor my law, but have rejected it.}* Or, *and as for my law, they have even*, (as before) or, *also*, (as ch. 1:3.) *rejected it*. So Isa. 5:24. ch. 8:9.

**Verse 20.** *{To what purpose cometh there to me incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices sweet unto me.}* Because this people might object, that they had not left God; for they served him still; they frequented his sanctuary with odors and offerings: God tells them, that their services were none of them pleasing to him; so long as their lives and courses otherwise were such as he had before showed. See the like, Isa. 1:11, 15. & 66:3. ch. 7:21, 26. Ezek. 20:39. Amos 5:21. Mic. 6:6, 10.

*{To what purpose cometh there to me incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country?}* The words thus rendered, sound, as if some such presents were from remote parts brought to God's temple; as Ps. 68:29, 31. Isa. 60:6, 7. Zeph. 3:10. whereas no such thing is intended; and the words therefore would rather thus be rendered, *To what purpose unto me* (that is, so far as concerns me) *is incense, that cometh from Sheba, or sweet cane that cometh from far*. See Isa. 1:11.

*{incense}* Such as you bring to burn before me. See Isa. 1:13.

*{cometh there}* Or, *that cometh*; a defect of the relative: as v. 15.

*{from Sheba}* See Isa. 60:6.

*{and the sweet cane}* Or, *or* (as ch. 2:18. & 5:12.) *sweet cane*. Heb. *cane the good*, or, *that is good*; or, *cane of the best*. See verses 13, 16. and that I take to be, as the native notion of the word; so the genuine sense of it in this place: of such *cane*, see Isa. 43:24. & Ezek. 27:19. where it is rendered, *calamus*.

*{from a far country}* Far fetched, because their own land afforded it not: the word *fetched*, or, *that cometh*, supplied from the former branch; as Gen. 1:16, 30. yet we need not with Jerome, and some others, travel so far as India to fetch it. Strabo tells us, that the Sabeans had store of such spices, *lib. 16.* and that might very well be termed a far country, Matt. 12:42.

*{your burnt offerings are not acceptable}* Heb. *to well-liking*, or, *acceptance*: as Isa. 56:7. & 60:7. See Isa. 1:11. ch. 7:21.

*{nor your sacrifices sweet unto me}* Heb. *and your sacrifices are not sweet*, or, *delightful, to me*: as Prov. 13:19. So Hos. 9:4.

**Verse 21.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will lay stumbling blocks before this people}* Heb. *Behold, I am giving, or, laying*, (as ch. 21:5. Lev. 19:14.) *stumblements* (if we might so speak; anything a man may stumble at. See Isa. 57:14.) *unto this people*: as, *come unto them*, for, *come before them*, Isa. 1:23. I will bring those things upon them, that shall be means of ruin and mischief to them. So Ezek. 3:20. & 7:19. Some suppose an allusion in the term to caltrops, and other like warlike engines, that are wont to be cast in the way to maim foot or horse, and cause them to fall: what is by them here intimated, see verse 22.

*{and the fathers and the sons together shall fall upon them}* Or, *shall stumble and fall by them*. See on v. 15. Isa. 3:8. they shall miscarry promiscuously one with another, v. 11. ch. 13:14. Howbeit, the rabbin seems to stretch it too far, who so understands it, as if it were meant, that they should tell or give warning of it, such as did see that which they should or might stumble at, one to another.

*{the neighbour and his friend shall perish.}* They shall so fall, that they shall not be able to recover, or get up again; but shall perish and miscarry, Isa. 8:14, 15.

**Verse 22.** *{Thus saith the LORD, Behold, a people cometh from the north country; and a great nation shall be raised from the sides of the earth.}* Or, *Behold a people coming*: as if he saw them on their march. So ch. 4:16. The Chaldeans' forces by which they should fall and miscarry, verse 21.

*{from the north}* As ch. 1:15. & 10:22. & 25:9.

*{a great nation}* Ch. 5:15.

*{shall be raised up}* As a storm is raised, ch. 25:32. and it is God himself that raises it: as the like, Isa. 13:17. ch. 50:9. & 51:1. Ezek. 23:22. See ch. 1:15.

*{from the sides of the earth}* As far as the king of Babylon's dominions reach, ch. 5:15. See the like terms, ch. 50:41. and this threatened, Deut. 28:49.

**Verse 23.** *{They shall lay hold on bow and spear:}* They shall be abundantly furnished with weapons to annoy and destroy with, both afar off, and at hand. See the like, ch. 50:42. So Ps. 35:2, 3. Yet by *spear*, some understand here the *staff* of the ensign, or standard: as Josh. 8:18, 26. But the joining of *bow* and it together, carries it rather the former and more frequent way.

*{they are cruel, and have no mercy}* Heb. *cruel is he*; (the pronoun for the verb substantive, as ch. 5:15, 16.) *cruel are they* each of them: as afterward, *and they will not pity*, ch. 21:7. See the like, Isa. 13:17, 18. ch. 50:42. and the thing fulfilled, 2 Chr. 36:17. as had been before threatened, Deut. 28:50.

*{their voice roareth like the sea}* See Isa. 5:30.

*{and they ride on horses,}* Heb. *on horses shall they ride*; not as those, to escape by flight, Isa. 30:16. but as ready to take the field, and well fitted for fight. So ch. 50:42.

*{set in array as a man for war,}* That is, as some, a people, or nation, (from v. 22.) *set in array as a man*: the whole nation as one man, as Judg. 20:8. or, *set every one in array, as a man for war*, or, *for battle*. So ch. 50:42. as if he saw them now not on their march, but in the field, and place of fight, ready to join battle, or make some assault.

*{against thee, O daughter of Zion}* As, *O daughter of Babylon*, ch. 50:42. See Isa. 1:8.

**Verse 24.** *{We have heard the fame thereof, our hands wax feeble; anguish hath taken hold of us, and pain as of a woman in travail.}* At the very first report of their approach, all will be dismayed, and quite out of heart. See ch. 4:9, 31. & 13:21.

**Verse 25.** *{Go not out into the field, nor walk by the way; for the sword of the enemy, and fear is on every side.}* The speeches of them that in those times should be one to another.

*{Go not out into the field}* Keep within the fenced cities and places of fastness, ch. 4:5, 6. & 8:14.

*{nor walk by the way}* Either stir not out at all; or, shun the common roads, and betake you to byways, as people are wont to do, when the passages are dangerous, Judg. 5:6. Isa. 33:17.

*{for the sword of the enemy, and fear is on every side.}* Or, as some, *the sword of the enemy is there; and fear on every side*: or, *for through*, (or, *by reason of*, the particle wanting; as Ps. 17:13, 14. & 44:2.) *the sword of the enemy*, (Lam. 5:9.) *there is fear on every side*: that which seems to have been a proverbial form of speech in frequent use among them, Ps. 31:13. ch. 20:3, 10. & 47:5. & 49:29.

**Verse 26.** *{O daughter of my people}* As ch. 4:11. v. 14.

*{gird thee with sackcloth,}* The common garb of mourners, ch. 4:8. & 25:34.

*{and wallow thyself in ashes:}* As on the most doleful occasions they were wont to do, Mic. 1:10.

*{make thee mourning, as for an only son}* Heb. *mourning of an only one make thee*: a defect of the substantive; as Prov. 4:3. See the like expressions, Amos 8:10. Zech. 12:10.

*{most bitter lamentation.}* Heb. *lamentation of bitternesses*; as, *weeping of bitternesses*, ch. 31:15. Of the former word, see ch. 4:8. The prophet so speaks, as if he could find no terms sufficient to describe such a lamentation, as the grievousness of their calamities might be deemed to deserve. See ch. 9:17, 18. for these plurals are wont much to exaggerate. See Isa. 58:9. ch. 9:17. & 14:1.

*{for the spoiler shall suddenly come upon us.}* Or, *is suddenly come upon us*; Nebuchadnezzar with his forces, ch. 48:8. See ch. 4:20.

**Verse 27.** *{I have set thee for a tower, and a fortress among my people, that thou mayest know, and try their way.}* Or, *To try have I set thee among my people as a fortress*. Or, which I take to be the genuine interpretation, *A fortified watchtower have I made thee among my people*. God's speech to the prophet; I the Lord have appointed you my prophet, (sufficiently supported and fenced, that you may not fear ought, ch. 1:18. & 15:20.) to be as a sentinel standing on a watchtower, Isa. 21:5, 8. Hab. 2:1. to espy, and descry, the dispositions, courses, and carriages of this people.

*{I have set thee}* Heb. *given thee*; as ch. 1:5. Ezek. 3:17.

*{for a tower}* Or, as some, *to try*, taking it for a verb; as Zech. 13:9. but the most otherwise: the word properly signifies a watchtower, whereupon sentinel is kept, to descry and discover the approach of ought that may prove prejudicial. See Isa. 23:13. and 32:14.

*{and a fortress}* Heb. *a fence*, or *fortification*; that is, as some interpreters not amiss supply from the former words, *a tower of fences or fortification*, that is, *a fenced, or fortified tower*: as, *a city of fences or fortification*, for, *a fenced, or fortified city*; as Ps. 108:11. ch. 1:18. & 5:17.

*{that thou mayest know, and try their way.}* To search and sift them, and to try them as a founder does metal, (for thereof also is the word used, Job 23:10. Ps. 66:10.) that you may by diligent observation of them, and their courses, descry and take notice of (as v. 18.) their affections and dispositions, be able to distinguish between the good and bad, and to work, if it may be, the wickedness of the wicked out of them, ch. 15:19. Heb. *and thou shalt know, and try*, or *search out, their way*, for, *that thou mayest so do*; as Josh. 24:9. Mal. 1:9. *Know and try*, for, *by trying know*: as, *search and try*, for, *by searching try*, Lam. 3:40. *make bald and poll*, for, *by polling make bald*, Mic. 1:16. *live and remain*, for, *remain alive*, 1 Thess. 4:17.

**Verse 28.** *{They are all grievous revolters}* The prophet's answer returned unto God, as rendering an account of the charge imposed on him, containing an exact censure of them, upon his search and survey. There is a grievous defection, and obstinacy therein, in the generality of them. Heb. *They are all* (as Isa. 60:21.) *revolters of revolters*, or *refractory ones*, that is, *grievous revolters*, or *extremely refractory*: as, *a servant of servants*, for, *a most base slave*, Gen. 9:25. and *wickedness of wickedness*, for, *extreme wickedness*, Hos. 10:15. See ch. 5:3, 23. Some of the Jewish doctors following the Chaldee, as also the old Latin, render it, *Princes of revolters*; and expound it, of great ones giving evil examples to the people, and making use of them, as instruments for the practice of wickedness, applying the next words to wrongful informations: but the initial letter is diverse (though in sound much the same, and in some words promiscuously used) nor will the text, without needless straining, bear it.

*{walking with slanders}* Heb. *walkers of detraction*. So ch. 9:5. such as make a trade of it, forbidden, Lev. 19:16.

*{they are brass and iron:}* Base metal, drossy matter; not any metal of price, gold or silver, to be found in them, which yet with the ore of those baser metals, is sometime, in some quantity, found mixed. See Isa. 1:21. Ezek. 22:18.

*{they are all corrupters}* Or, *corrupt*: both corrupt themselves and corrupting one another, see Isa. 1:4.

**Verse 29.** *{The bellows are burnt, the lead is consumed of the fire, the founder melteth in vain, for the wicked are not plucked away.}* All the labor and pains that has been taken by God and his prophets, for the refining and reforming of them, is lost; it is but labor in vain, they are no whit the better for it, Isa. 49:4. ch. 2:30.

*{The bellows are burnt}* The prophet prosecutes the similitude taken from the practice of metalists, in trying and melting of their ore. By the *bellows*, some understand God's chastisements; some, his Spirit; neither well fitting here. Others, the prophet's tongue and throat, according to that, Ps. 22:15. & 69:3. I should rather say their lungs, not unlike bellows, and with much speech and clamor wasted. But unto such particularities, in allegories, we need not descend.

*{the lead is consumed of the fire}* Or, as some, *the tin* (so termed, because used for separation of metals, as quicksilver in these times, Isa. 1:25.) *is spent*, as Gen. 47:18. but *lead* and *tin* are distinguished, Ezek. 22:20. and the Jewish commenters tell us, that lead was also in their times made use of, in fining of silver, to melt it the more easily, and with least loss, or waste. Howbeit, an interpreter of prime note, reads the text thus, *The bellows are burnt with the fire: the whole is lead*: there is nothing but drossy matter that, upon melting, appears: and this should I incline to, were there any instance of the like.

*{the founder melteth in vain;}* Heb. *in vain melting melteth he*; or, *trying trieth he*: take he never so much pains in melting and trying, though he do it never so diligently and exquisitely, all is to no purpose. See the like, Ps. 58:5. the word *founder* is not in the text, but is included in the verb, and from it supplied; as Gen. 50:26. *they embalmed him*, that is, *the embalmers embalmed him*; as it is more fully there, v. 2.

*{for the wicked are not plucked away.}* Or, *for their wickednesses*. Heb. *and* (as ch. 3:24. & 5:2.) *evil*, or *evils*, (*evil things*, as Ps. 78:49.) *will not*, or *cannot*, (as ch. 2:23.) *be removed*, or *withdrawn*, (as the word is rendered, Josh. 8:16. Judg. 20:32.) *from them*; a double defect of the pronoun, both positive, and possessive, as vv. 3, 12. Gen. 43:24. Isa. 13:8, 19.

**Verse 30.** *{Reprobate silver shall men call them:}* Or, *Refuse*, or *Rejected silver* (such as is nothing but refuse, or dross; or such as is refused, and will not pass in payment; opposed to current coin, such as will pass without refusal, Gen. 23:16. and it agrees well with the Greek word, that signifies *counterfeit*, or *disallowed*, 2 Cor. 13:5, 6. where the mistranslating of it has stumbled many) *shall they be called*. Heb. *shall they call them*; as Mal. 1:4. for *men*, is not in the text. See Isa. 1:22. Prov. 20:23. Lam. 3:45. So Ps. 15:4. *a vile man is in his sight as refuse*.

*{for the LORD hath rejected them.}* Lam. 5:22. Hos. 9:17. because they have rejected him, and his word, Isa. 5:24. verse 19. ch. 8:9. See ch. 2:37.

## CHAPTER 7

**Verse 1.** *{The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying.}* At this chapter begins a new sermon or prophecy, carried on to the end of chapter 9. In this the prophet labors to beat them off from their vain confidence in the temple and services therein performed, verses 2, 12. by setting before them the example of Shiloh, where the tabernacle sometime was, verses 13, 15. by showing what account God made of their sacrifices, being joined with willful disobedience, verses 21, 28. and for their continued idolatries, threatens them with utter destruction unavoidable, verses 16, 20. and that so great, that they would want room to bury their corpses, verses 29, 34. Of the words of this verse, see on ch. 1:2.

**Verse 2.** *{Stand in the gate of the LORD's house, and proclaim there this word, and say, Hear the word of the LORD, all ye of Judah, that enter in at these gates, to worship the LORD.}*

*{Stand}* Not *sit*; for they *sat* there to hear causes, ch. 26:10. they *stood* to preach, or deliver prophecies, ch. 26:2.

*{in the gate}* Or, *in the porch*, or *at the entry*: that which opened into the great court, where the people used to meet. See ch. 26:2, 10. & 36:10.

*{the LORD's house}* The temple, ch. 26:5. vv. 4, 10.

*{proclaim there}* There was he the rather to deliver this message, because to refel the fond conceit, that they had of that place, as a sufficient shelter and safeguard for them, though they were never so loose and licentious in their lives, vv. 8, 9.

*{this word}* Or, *this matter*: as 1 Sam. 3:17. ch. 5:14.

*{Hear the word of the LORD}* As ch. 2:4.

*{all ye of Judah}* Heb. *all Judah*: for out of all parts they used to resort thither, so long as the temple stood, Ps. 84:7. & 122:4. and it may be, that this prophecy was delivered at one of those solemn feasts, wherein all the males of the land in general were to meet there, Exod. 23:14, 17.

*{at these gates}* To go into the great court, the people's court, distinguished from the priests' court, 2 Chr. 4:9. See ch. 36:10.

**Verse 3.** *{Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel,}* As Isa. 1:24. So v. 21. ch. 9:15.

*{Amend your ways, and your doings, and I will make you to dwell in this place}* Heb. *Make good your ways.* So verse 5. ch. 18:11. & 26:13.

*{make you to dwell}* *Continue your dwelling*; as, *make to live*, for, *continue in life*, Exod. 1:17.

*{in this place.}* Not in the temple, but in the land that you now possess, Ps. 37:3. v. 7. so Isa. 36:10.

**Verse 4.** *{Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD are these.}* Heb. *Trust not to you* (an elegant redundancy, very frequent in Scripture, see ch. 4:12. & 5:5.) *in words*, or *matters*, (as vv. 2, 22.) *of falsehood*; as ch. 14:14. & 23:26. in such thoughts and conceits, as will fail you, and frustrate your expectations, verse 8. ch. 4:14. & 29:31. Trust not to the temple, and the services there performed, as if these things could secure you. See the like, ch. 18:18. Mic. 3:11. 1 Cor. 10:1, 5.

*{the temple of the LORD are these.}* Or, *These are the Lord's palaces*; as Ps. 11:4. and so the word properly signifies, Ps. 45:15. Isa. 39:7. Not *this people*, (as some fondly would have it) *are God's temple*, 1 Cor. 3:16, 17. & 6:19. but *these* buildings, which with the finger he seemed to point to; as they, Matt. 24:1, 2. see ch. 10:11. as if he had said, These thoughts you have in your hearts, and these, or the like words oft in your mouths. These buildings, the two courts, the house, and the oracle, were by Solomon built, at God's appointment, for his place of constant and continual residence, which he will therefore hold and uphold forever, Ps. 132:14. 2 Chr. 33:7, 8. the pronoun positive, for the verb substantive; as ch. 6:23, 28.
