This threefold repetition, though it have an emphasis in it, as well as that, Isaiah 6:3. & ch. 22:29. yet I suppose not so much to import the excellency of the temple, or estimation of it with God, as the frequency of these terms in the mouths of the people: and much less to aim at any curious distribution of it into the house, the courts, and the outer edifices about either, as some would have it: or that the people themselves should by this threefold repetition have some reference to the three times of their solemn appearance yearly in that place, Exod. 23:14, 17. as the Chaldee expresses it.

**Verse 5.** *{For if ye thoroughly amend your ways, and your doings; if ye thoroughly execute judgment between a man and his neighbour;}* A promise of continuance, upon condition of reformation, in matter as well of justice and equity, as of piety and godliness.

*{thoroughly amend}* Or, *surely*, or *seriously amend*. Heb. *making good make good*; as verse 3.

*{thoroughly execute}* Or, *sedulously exercise*. Heb. *doing do judgment*, or *right*. See ch. 5:1. & 22:4.

*{between a man and his neighbour}* That is, *between man and man*; as ch. 22:8. Heb. *between a man and between his neighbor*; as, *between the light, and between the darkness*, Gen. 1:4, 18. a redundancy frequent in Hebrew. So John 10:18. *I have power to lay down my life, and I have power to take it up again*; that is, *I have power, having laid down my life, to take it up again*.

**Verse 6.** *{If ye oppress not the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow}* Or, *Oppress not any stranger, orphan, or widow*; carrying it on with the former, v. 5. *and*, for, *or*; as Exod. 21:15. persons that God has taken more specially into his protection, and given a special charge of, Exod. 22:21, 24. Deut. 10:18. & 27:19.

*{and shed not innocent blood in this place}* Or, *not shed innocent blood*; the guilt whereof, how grievous, see 2 Kings 24:4. *in this place*; in Jerusalem, or the land you live in; as v. 3. see Num. 35:31, 33.

*{neither walk after other gods to your hurt}* *Other gods*; as ch. 1:17. *to your hurt*, or, *to your own hurt*; as ch. 5:19. and so, *their own faces*, v. 19. Heb. *to evil to you*; that is, *to your own evil*: not to any evil, or hurt, that shall accrue to me by it, but all to yourselves. See v. 19. God is neither the better for man's obedience, nor the worse for man's wickedness: neither does his goodness, or badness, reach unto God, Ps. 16:2. Job 22:2, 3. & 35:5, 8.

**Verse 7.** *{Then will I cause you to dwell in this place}* As v. 3. Heb. *And*; as ch. 4:1, 2.

*{in the land that I gave unto your fathers for ever and ever.}* Heb. *to from of old, and for ever*; which some, so rendering, refer it unto *gave*, and expound it of the time past from Joshuah's days, by whom God put them at first in possession of it, wherein they had continued unto that time: or, as others rather, *from age unto age*; referring it, as our version does, unto the word *dwell*, and understanding it of continuance for time to come, from age to age, in the land, upon performance of the condition here propounded. So ch. 25:5. The Jewish critics observe well a redundancy of the former *to* here, as elsewhere, Deut. 9:7. Judg. 19:30. ch. 31:34. and so verse 25.

**Verse 8.** *{Behold}* Consider and think seriously of it; as verses 6, 19.

*{ye trust in lying words that cannot profit.}* Heb. *ye are trusting to you* (such a redundancy, as ch. 4:12. & 11:17. Ezek. 37:11.) *in words of falsehood* (as verse 4.) *to not profit*, or *no profit*; as Isa. 44:10. This some understand of the false prophets' lies and flatteries, which they were too much taken with, and trusted unto, ch. 5:31. & 6:13, 14. & 23:26. & 28:15. & 29:31. but it seems rather to have reference to what went before, verse 4. you trust in vain, to no purpose, on that which will not avail you, nor stand you in any stead.

**Verse 9.** *{Will ye steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not?}* Will you live in continual practice of iniquity, immanity, impurity, and impiety? Or, *when as ye steal*, etc. Heb. *stealing ye steal*: and so constantly in all the rest; for they are all infinitives: of the phrase of speech, see on Isa. 59:13. and it is very emphatic; when as you make a common practice of these things. The like syntax, see ch. 2:20. & 5:7.

*{swear falsely}* Heb. *swear to falsehood*; as ch. 5:2.

*{burn incense to Baal}* See ch. 2:23. & 11:13.

*{walk after other gods}* Verse 6. ch. 11:10. & 13:10.

*{which ye know not}* Or, *which ye have not known*; which you have not formerly had any notice of, nor have been acquainted with in former times, Deut. 28:61. called therefore *new gods*, Judg. 5:8. Others, of whom you have had no such proof or experience, as of me you have had: and that follows well from the former; but the former seems the first, proper, and genuine sense. See Isaiah 43:10.

**Verse 10.** *{And come and stand before me in this house which is called by my name}* Or, according to the syntax before hinted; *when as ye steal*, etc. *Will ye come and stand before me in this house*, etc. See the like construction, Isa. 30:20. and 35:4. and 37:9.

*{come}* Repair to my sanctuary. See Ezek. 23:38, 39.

*{stand before me}* After the manner of servants, attending upon me, as your Lord. See 1 Kings 10:8. and 17:1. Prov. 22:29.

*{in this house}* The temple, verses 2, 4.

*{which is called by my name}* That bears my name, is called and accounted my house. Heb. *which my name is called upon it*; or, *whereupon my name is called*. So verses 11, 14, 30. ch. 32:34.

*{and say, We are delivered to do all these abominations?}* *We are delivered*: or, as some render it, *We shall be delivered to do all these abominable things*; that is, say they, That we may return again, having by sacrifices, and other external rites, expiated the guilt of our former excesses, to commit and practice them afresh as freely as ever; as the common sort of people, in many Popish places, are reported to use it as a byword; *We must sin to be shriven, and shriven to sin.* Or, as others, Notwithstanding that we have committed such things, yet shall we be safe, and do well enough for all that. See Mal. 3:15. But neither will the words bear the latter; nor does the former seem to express the right sense of the place: which the pauses, in the original, being well observed, will lead us to: the middle pause is at, *We are delivered*: and there ends their speech: the words following are the prophet's, uttered in the person of God; not theirs. So the meaning is, *Will ye when ye have robbed, and killed, and committed adultery, and perjury, and idolatry, come and present yourselves before me in mine house, and say, We are delivered*; that is, discharged of the guilt of these our sins (so is the word used, Ps. 39:8. & 51:14.) *that ye may return to the practice of these vile courses afresh?* For I cannot assent to that learned late writer, who would remove here the interrogative out of his wonted and constant office, and make it a note, either of asseveration, or of demonstration, both here, and elsewhere, Gen. 27:36. 1 Sam. 2:27. 2 Sam. 23:19. 1 Kings 16:31. Prov. 24:28. in most of which places, the interrogative is generally admitted, and does right well.

**Verse 11.** *{Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes?}* Do you account my house, my palace, to be a hole, or a hold, for thieves and robbers, to shroud and shelter themselves in? Matt. 21:13. Mark 11:17. Luke 19:46. and that by performance of some formalities there, you are not only discharged of the guilt of your former sins, but have liberty to sin afresh? and so make me both a patron of your base and abominable courses, and a pander also thereunto? whereas I abhor and abominate both your wicked ways, and these your thoughts; and all your sacrifices and services the rather for them. See Prov. 15:8, 9, 26. & 21:27. Isaiah 61:8.

*{a den}* An allusion to such dens and caves, where either wild beasts, or men mischievously minded, are wont to lie in wait to seize upon passengers; and whereunto they repair with their prey, and their spoil, Ps. 10:8, 9. Nah. 2:12.

*{robbers}* The word signifies properly *a burglar*, one that breaks open houses, Ezek. 7:22. but it is more generally used for persons that spoil and plunder, Dan. 11:14. and for beasts that live by spoil and prey, Isa. 35:9.

*{in your eyes}* Heb. *is it in your eyes*; that is, do you so account it? or think you that I can endure to have my house so esteemed. See the same phrase, Num. 13:33. 1 Sam. 18:23.

*{Behold, even I have seen it, saith the LORD.}* I see these your abominable courses, as closely, and covertly, as you carry them, Ps. 10:11, 14. Ezek. 8:12. and these your impious thoughts too, of me and my sacrifice, Ps. 94:7, 11. So ch. 13:27. and 23:14.

**Verse 12.** *{But go ye now unto my place, which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first; and see what I did to it, for the wickedness of my people Israel.}* God refutes this their vain confidence in the fabric of the temple, by an instance from another place that sometime had the like privilege, that had the tabernacle, and the ark with it, as they now had the temple; but that did not secure them when they grew wicked.

*{go ye now}* His meaning is not that they should travel thither, but go thither only in their thoughts. See the like, ch. 2:10. Amos 6:2.

*{to my place}* That which was once my place, as this is now; called therefore, *his house*, Judg. 18:31. Ps. 42:4.

*{in Shiloh}* Or, *at Shiloh*; a city belonging to the tribe of Ephraim, Ps. 78:60, 67. situate, as may seem, between Bethel, and Shechem, Judg. 21:19.

*{where I set my name at the first}* Heb. *where I made*, or *caused, my name to dwell*: as Deut. 12:11. where I at first in Joshua's time placed those visible pledges of my special presence and residence among you, Josh. 18:1. 1 Sam. 1:3, 7. & 4:3, 4.

*{and see}* Take notice of, and consider; as ch. 2:19. and 6:16.

*{what I did to it}* How I forsook that place, and fixed my abode in another; having first suffered my people to be discomfited by the enemy; my priests to be slain, mine ark to be carried away captive, which albeit it were after some time sent home again, yet never returned any more unto Shiloh, 1 Sam. 2:10, 11. & 7:1, 2. Ps. 78:59, 67.

*{for the wickedness of my people}* Proceeding principally from the priests, 1 Sam. 2:12, 17, 22, 34. See the like advertisements, ch. 3:7, 8. & 44:2, 3.

**Verse 13.** *{And now because ye have done all these works, saith the LORD; and I spake unto you, rising early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not.}* Since that you do wickedly as they did, and will take no warning, I will deal with you, as I dealt with them.

*{rising early}* From time to time diligently addressing myself unto you by my prophets: a form of speech taken from the wonted manner of sedulous and industrious either tradesmen, or workmen, that get up betimes before daylight, to follow their employments. See on ch. 5:8. So verse 25. ch. 11:7. & 25:3. & 35:15. See Isaiah 65:2.

*{I called you, but ye answered not}* You regarded not my call, inviting you to repentance, that you might prevent and escape ruin. So Prov. 1:24. Isa. 50:2. & 65:12. & 66:4.

**Verse 14.** *{Therefore will I do unto this house which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place, which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh:}* Heb. *And I will do*, as ch. 6:11.

*{to this house}* Which yet is but a house; and a house that cannot hold me, 1 Kings 8:27. Isa. 66:1.

*{which is called by my name}* Which I am pleased yet to own, so long as I please, and no longer. See v. 10.

*{wherein ye trust}* But in vain, vv. 4, 8.

*{unto the place}* Not to my sanctuary alone, where at present I dwell, Ps. 132:13. but to the whole land also wherein you dwell, verses 3, 7.

*{which I gave you}* And therefore can take again from you, when I please, Job 1:21. for it is mine still, and you are but sojourners in it with me, Lev. 25:23. and it was given both to you, and your ancestors, upon condition, that you should keep my statutes, and observe my laws, Ps. 104:44, 45. which you do not, but the contrary, verses 9, 13.

*{as I have done to Shiloh}* Which I forsook, Ps. 78:60. ch. 26:6.

**Verse 15.** *{And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.}* I will carry you away captive out of that land, wherein I have formerly in a gracious manner resided among you, Ps. 76:1, 2. Heb. *from against*, or, *over against, my face*: as those things are, that are before a man, and whereon he fixes his eye. So Exod. 20:2. 1 Kings 9:7.

*{as I have cast out}* Sent into captivity by Salmaneser, 2 Kings 17:6.

*{your brethren}* That were the seed of Israel, as well as yourselves; and you have no reason therefore to look to fare better than they, when you do as they did, 2 Kings 21:13, 14.

*{the whole seed of Ephraim}* The ten tribes bearing the name of Ephraim, as the principal among them. See Isa. 7:2.

**Verse 16.** *{Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry, nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear.}* The Lord here turns his speech from them to the prophet; and to intimate, that he was resolved to put in execution the doom forementioned upon them, notwithstanding their vain hopes and confidence of the contrary; forbids the prophet to strike in between him and them, by any intercession in their behalf, to stay his hand from proceeding against them, as Moses did, Exod. 32:32. Num. 14:13, 19. and Aaron, Num. 16:47, 48. Ps. 106:23. See the like, Exod. 32:10. ch. 11:14. & 14:11.

*{Therefore}* Or, *wherefore*. Heb. *And*; as v. 14.

*{for I will not hear thee}* Showing how little hope there is, that the prayers of the godly should prevail with God, for those that persist obstinately in sinful courses, rejecting the means of mercy tendered unto them, and pressed upon them, 1 Sam. 14:35. ch. 15:1.

**Verse 17.** *{Seest thou not what they do in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?}* Are not you yourself an eyewitness of those abominable idolatries, that all sorts of them, men, women and children, in all places among them commit? See ch. 2:28. & 11:13. Heb. *Art thou not seeing?* Is it not a continual eyesore to you; as the Sodomites' manner of life was to Lot? 2 Pet. 2:7, 8.

**Verse 18.** *{The children gather the wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven}* Fathers and children, husbands and wives, find all some employment or other, about their idolatrous services. See ch. 44:17, 19.

*{children}* Thus idolatrous parents train up their children in idolatry: let Christian parents learn from them to train up theirs in piety. Gen. 18:19. Deut. 6:7. Prov. 4:3, 4. & 22:6. Eph. 6:4. 1 Tim. 4:6. 2 Tim. 3:15.

*{gather}* Heb. *gathering*; and so, *kindling*, and *kneading*: and so it may be retained; as having reference to verse 17. *Seest thou not—the children gathering sticks, and the fathers kindling the fire, and the women kneading dough?* or, how (supplied, ch. 3:6.) *the children are gathering sticks, and the fathers are kindling the fire, and the women are kneading dough?* as noting how busily they were employed about it. So Matt. 24:38. See ch. 6:28.

*{wood}* The word is plural; rendered sticks, Num. 15:32, 33. and so would be rather here, than there.

*{kindle the fire}* To bake with it; as he to roast, Isa. 44:16.

*{knead their dough}* Heb. no more then, *Kneading dough*; nor needs any more. So Hos. 7:4.

*{to make cakes}* The word is nowhere else found save here, and ch. 44:18. they are said by some of the Jewish critics, to have been so termed, from the *figure* of a star that was imprinted upon them; to the honor of which they were made, to offer and present thereunto, Amos 5:26. Howbeit, some other would have them so termed from the curious preparation of them; and others, from the use of fire about the dressing of them, deducing it from a word that signifies *to burn*. It is hard to give any certain sentence, where so little light to guide.

*{to the queen of heaven}* There is a twofold reading here; for some read the word without an *Aleph*, and then it should signify *a queen*; though in this form, that word be nowhere found: but yet thus divers of the Jewish doctors, and the old Latin, whom many others follow, here take it; conceiving thereby to be understood, some the *sun*; the words that signify it, being one of them less frequent, of a feminine form, Isa. 24:23. the other more usual, though of a masculine form, yet a feminine oft in use; as Nahum 3:17. Others, the *moon*: one name whereof is feminine; though another be masculine: and which the Phoenicians, say some, from the Hebrew call *Baaltis*, and *Baltis*. Others, some great *star*; but what, or which, they tell us not: and this way the Chaldee takes; and that the idolatrous Jews did worship both the *sun* and the *moon*, is not to be doubted. See ch. 8:2. Howbeit, because this word is never found used in that notion, (and yet the form is not irregular; and they might well of purpose so frame it, to make a sacred term of it) the Jewish critics most of them, and others of ours following them read the word with an *Aleph*; in which form it is very commonly found used for *work*, or workmanship, as Exod. 36:5. 2 Chr. 13:10. ch. 48:11. and so render it, *the frame*, or *workmanship of heaven*; and the ancient Greek, *the host of heaven*; which seems to receive some strength from the collation of this place with that, ch. 19:13. the name of *host* being used there, instead of that here. The words then may be read, both here, and ch. 44:17. *for the queen*, or, *the frame, of heaven*: as, *a footstool for thy feet*, Ps. 110:1. and, *a place for the Lord*, Ps. 132:5.

*{and to pour out drink offerings unto other gods}* Both this and the former helping, in likelihood, to furnish that table, which for such feigned deities they used to spread, Isa. 65:11. whereof also some expound this place. In those *cakes*, they imitated God's *meat*, or, *meal*, offerings; in these, his *drink-offerings*: of both which, see Lev. 2:4, 5, 7. Num. 28:7, 8. Isa. 1:13. & 57:6. Of *other gods*, see ch. 1:16.

*{that they may provoke me to anger}* Heb. *to anger me*. So 2 Kings 22:17. 2 Chr. 34:25. ch. 11:17. & 25:7. & 32:29. Not that they did these things purposely for that end; but that this could not but necessarily thence ensue. See on Isa. 3:8. and see the like, ch. 27:10. Hos. 8:4.

**Verse 19.** *{Do they provoke me to anger, saith the LORD? do they not provoke themselves to the confusion of their own faces?}* Some render the words; *Is it against me that they provoke me to wrath? is it not rather against themselves, to the confusion of their own faces?* as if he had said, Am I any whit the worse for it? does it not rather tend to their own ruins? the sense is good: see on verse 6. and the matter such as is implied; but the words will not admit it: the text is word for word thus; *Do they anger me? saith the Lord: not themselves to the confusion of their own faces?* and there is an elegant *antanaclasis*, or variation of notion, in one and the same term: as if it were said; they do not so much provoke me to anger, as procure anger to themselves; by angering me, they but anger themselves, or, as we use to say, they do but spite themselves, and bring shame and confusion upon themselves. See 1 Cor. 10:22. Of confusion of face, see ch. 3:25. Ps. 44:15. Dan. 9:8. *their own faces*: as, *their own ways*, Isa. 53:6. So ch. 4:18. v. 6.

**Verse 20.** *{Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Mine anger and my fury shall be poured forth upon this place, upon man, and upon beast, and upon the trees of the field, and upon the fruit of the ground; and it shall burn, and shall not be quenched.}* Since that they will needs be thus angering me, I will anger them to the purpose; and they shall find by feeling to their cost, who it is that smarts for it, that suffers by it: and since that they will needs be thus incensing my wrath, it shall be so forced, that it shall waste all with them, and none shall be able to quench it again. See the like, Deut. 32:21, 22.

*{Mine anger}* Which they have provoked and raised, v. 18.

*{my fury}* Or, *wrath*; or, *fervor*: my fierce or fiery indignation. See ch. 4:4.

*{shall be poured forth}* As ch. 10:25. as the clouds or heavens are said to pour down water, when they shoot down showers of rain in great abundance, Ps. 77:17. an allusion to those showers of fire and brimstone, that burnt up Sodom and Gomorrah, Gen. 19:24. Ps. 11:6. See Ps. 78:49.

*{upon this place}* Not this city alone, but the whole land, v. 7.

*{upon man, and upon beast, and upon the trees of the field, and upon the fruit of the ground.}* A judgment parallel to those of Egypt, Exod. 9:3, 6, 18, 19, 25. & 10:5, 15. Ps. 78:45, 48. & 105:33, 36. such an utter desolation and destruction of all, as is described, ch. 4:25. & 12:4. Zeph. 1:3.

*{it shall burn and shall not be quenched}* When God's wrath is once thoroughly kindled, it is not so easy quenching of it again. Ps. 2:12. See ch. 4:4.

**Verse 21.** *{Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel,}* As verse 2. The Lord turns his speech now to the people again. And because their vain confidence was partly in the temple, and partly in the sacrifices that thither they brought and there offered; God therefore to beat them off also from this; as before he showed what he would do with that house, verse 14. so now he gives them to understand what account he made of all their sacrifices, what sorry acceptance they had at his hands.

*{Put your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat flesh}* Keep your sacrifices to yourselves, dispose of them as you please: eat yourselves the flesh as well of one sort of them, as of the other: I neither require any from you, nor delight in any of them, nor desire them, nor regard them. See Isa. 1:11. ch. 6:20. Amos 5:21.

*{Put your burnt offerings to your sacrifices}* Your *holocausts* that were to be all burnt, Lev. 1:9. to your other *sacrifices*, whether *pacificatory*, or, *gratulatory*, *voluntary*, or, *votary*, whereof some part the offerers themselves might eat, Lev. 7:11, 12, 15, 16. take them, and put them all together; I desire no part or share in any at all of them.

*{and eat flesh}* Eat their *flesh*; or *the flesh* of them: a defect of the possessive; as ch. 6:3, 12.

**Verse 22.** *{For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings, or sacrifices.}* Not that God did not then take order for, and give in charge, the due performance of these sacred rites, Lev. 17. but that these were not the things that he principally regarded, or chiefly required: it was not so much these ceremonial performances, as their cordial affection and constant obedience thence proceeding that he required of them, and looked for from them, 1 Sam. 15:22. Ps. 50:5, 16. Mark 12:33, 50. Hos. 6:6. Matt. 12:7. *I desire mercy, and not sacrifice*; that is, not so much sacrifice as mercy: and, *rent your hearts, and not your garments*; that is, not so much your garments as your hearts, Joel 2:13. For I can in no wise assent unto those, (though I find among the ancients divers of the same mind with them) who suppose, that the use of sacrificing was at first but an humane invention, and that God only gave way to it, to prevent a worse matter; because otherwise men would be doing it to idols and devils, Lev. 17:7. The antiquity of it, even from Adam, Gen. 4:3, 4. the constant practice of it among God's people in all ages, Gen. 8:20. & 12:7. & 35:7. Exod. 5:3. & 8:27. the strict and solemn enacting of it, with an exact injunction and determination of so many observations and circumstances about it; and the prefiguration of future accomplishments represented in it, Heb. 9. & 10. do evidently evince the practice of this rite, to have been from the beginning a divine institution; which the devil, God's ape, as well in this, as in other sacred ordinances of God imitating, did after arrogate to himself.

*{concerning}* Heb. *concerning the word*, or, *matter*, of them: as Est. 9:26, 31. ch. 5:2, 34. So also, ch. 5:28. vv. 2, 4, 8.

*{in the day that}* Or, *what time*; *when*: as Gen. 3:17. Ruth 4:5. 1 Kings 2:37. Heb. *in the day of my making them to go forth*; and so ch. 11:4.

**Verse 23.** *{But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice; and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people.}* The main matter, that God first and principally required then of them, was *obedience*, Exod. 19:5, 6. and the sacrifices afterward, as a testification of their obedience and allegiance to him, and an obsignation of the covenant, concerning the same, plighted between him and them, in the blood of the Messias, Exod. 24:3, 8. Matt. 26:28. Luke 22:20. Heb. 9:19, 20.

*{this thing}* Heb. *word*: as Est. 1:21. & 2:4.

*{Obey}* Heb. *Hear*. So Exod. 15:26. Deut. 6:3. v. 24.

*{and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well with you}* So Deut. 5:29, 33. See v. 6.

*{in all the ways}* Heb. *in every way*; as Deut. 5:33.

**Verse 24.** *{But they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear; but walked in the counsels, and in the imagination of their evil heart, and went backward, and not forward.}* By solemn covenant this they engaged themselves unto, Exod. 19:8. & 24:3. Deut. 5:28. but they were not careful to make it good, Exod. 22:8. Deut. 9:24. & 31:27.

*{But}* Heb. *And*: as ch. 6:16. and so after again.

*{inclined their ear}* As the manner is of those that listen to ought, which they are desirous to hear. So ch. 11:8. and 17:23.

*{in the counsels}* Or, *contrivements*, or, *devices*. So Ps. 81:12.

*{imagination of their evil heart}* See ch. 3:17.

*{they went backward, and not forward.}* Heb. *they were to backward and not to face*: that which he said before, ch. 2:27. *they turned their back unto me, and not their face*.

**Verse 25.** *{Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day, I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early, and sending them.}* A defect of the pronoun: as ch. 6:29. I have not from time to time failed to advise and admonish both you and your ancestors by my ministers and messengers of those things that concern your duty and your welfare, Deut. 18:18. Amos 2:11. See on v. 13.

*{Since}* Or, *From*. Heb. *To from*: as v. 7.

*{I have even sent}* Or, *I have sent*; for the copulative here is as oft elsewhere redundant: as Jon. 1:1.

**Verse 26.** *{Yet they hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear; but hardened their neck, they did worse than their fathers.}* A change of the person, very frequent in this prophet; as ch. 2:7. & 5:19, 21. & 6:17. As if God unwilling to speak further to them, or loath to talk any longer with them, should turn his speech to the prophet, telling him how crossly and perversely they had carried themselves towards him. So ch. 44:10.

*{Yet}* Heb. *And*; as ch. 5:10, 22.

*{hearkened not}* Or, *have not hearkened*, Dan. 9:6, 10.

*{but}* Heb. *and*: as v. 24.

*{hardened their neck}* Or, *have stiffened*; whence the term of *stiff-necked*, Deut. 9:6. See Isa. 48:4. so ch. 16:12. & 17:23. & 19:15.

*{did worse than their fathers}* Or, *have done worse*. Heb. *have done evil from their fathers*; that is, worse than they. So Judg. 2:19. ch. 16:12. thus have they proceeded from evil to worse, ch. 9:3. so far are they from amendment.

**Verse 27.** *{Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them, but they will not answer thee.}* Or, *And though thou speak all these things* (as verse 23.) *to them, they will not hearken to thee: yea, though thou cry unto them, they will not answer thee*. So verse 13. Of this syntax, and such use of the copulatives, see ch. 2:5, 20. & 5:7. & 6:9, 10. Howbeit, true it is, that God will have his messengers and ministers, to speak, admonish, and warn, and do their duty, whether that people will hear and take warning, or no, to render them the more inexcusable, Ezek. 2:5, 7. & 3:7, 12.

**Verse 28.** *{But thou shalt say unto them, This is a nation that obeyeth not the voice of the LORD their God, nor receiveth correction:}* Or, *Therefore*: for the illative does better here, than before, v. 27. Heb. *And*: as verses 1, 4, 16.

*{obey not}* Or, *will not hear*. Heb. *hear not*; as v. 23. and the verb is plural, because the noun *nation* is collective.

*{nor receiveth correction}* Or, *nor receive*, or, *will receive instruction*. See ch. 2:30. & 5:3.

*{truth is perished, and is cut off from their mouth.}* There is no truth, or true dealing, to be expected from them, Ps. 5:9. & 12:1, 2. Isa. 59:14, 15. ch. 9:3. Hos. 4:1. See Ps. 119:43.

**Verse 29.** *{Cut off thine hair, O Jerusalem, and cast it away,}* This is spoken to Jerusalem, as to a woman, (for the verbs are feminine) inviting her to lamentation, and to external expressions of it, in regard of the calamities that were to befall her. It was the manner with them, in those times, for men in occasions of mourning, to cut off their hair, or shave their heads. So Job 1:20. Isa. 15:2. but it is a sign of greater grief, and deeper mourning, when women tear off, or cut off, and cast away, their hair, being deemed a principal ornament with them, Isa. 3:24. 1 Cor. 11:15. 1 Tim. 2:9. and this it is that is here alluded unto; as also, Mic. 1:16. and there is an emphasis in the word; for it signifies *a crown*: nor is it used of hair, or applied thereunto, save in the narrative of the *Nazarites*, Num. 6. and when she is bid therefore *to cut off her hair*, under the name of *a crown*; and not to cut it off only, and reserve it, as many are wont to do with their combings, and the like; but *to throw it away*, to cast it upon the ground; it seems to intimate that which our prophet bewails in the person of his people, *The crown is fallen from our head*, Lam. 5:16. and which the psalmist has more full; *Thou hast profaned his crown by casting it to the ground*, Ps. 89:39. So I should rather apply it, than with a learned late writer, to imply the dispersion of them into foreign parts; as that, Ezek. 5:2.

*{and take up a lamentation on high places}* *A lamentation*, see ch. 9:10, 20. *on the high places*, see ch. 3:21. for I cannot accord to that learned man, who in this place also would have it to be, *in the valleys*, or *on the plains*: see the like, ch. 12:12.

*{for the LORD hath rejected, and forsaken the generation of his wrath.}* He has cast off, as they have cast off him, (ch. 6:30. verse 15.) this whole race, against whom his wrath has been incensed by their sins, vv. 18, 20. See Mal. 1:4.

**Verse 30.** *{For the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, saith the LORD}* A passage again, from person to person, as before, verse 26.

*{For}* Or, *Because*; as ch. 6:13.

*{the children of Judah}* Either the posterity of Judah; as Joshua 14:6. or, the people of Judea; as, *the children of Noph*, ch. 2:16.

*{have done evil in my sight}* Or, *have done that which is evil in my sight*. Heb. *in mine eyes*; as 2 Sam. 11:27. either, done evil to my face, where I see it, v. 11. or, done those things that are displeasing to me. See Isa. 65:12. & 66:4.

*{they have set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to pollute it.}* They have set their idols in my palace: whereof, see verses 10, 11. not content to have them in their houses, or elsewhere abroad, Isa. 57:6, 7. ch. 19:13. they have brought them into mine house also, to set them cheek by jowl beside me, Ezek. 43:7, 8. see 2 Kings 16:10, 11, 15. & 21:4, 7. 2 Chr. 36:14. ch. 32:34.

**Verse 31.** *{And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, which I commanded them not, neither came it into mine heart.}* See the same, ch. 19:5.

*{built the high places}* Erected altars, and other structures, for the practice of that barbarous and most abominable idolatry, 2 Kings 21:3. & 23:10.

*{of Tophet}* Hereof, see on Isa. 30:33.

*{in the valley of the son of Hinnom}* A vale near to Jerusalem, whereof one Hinnom was sometime, and his sons after him, possessed; whose name therefore it bare in succeeding ages, and does still, in the sacred records, unto this day. See Josh. 15:8.

*{to burn their sons and their daughters}* See this savage and unnatural practice, 2 Kings 16:3. & 21:6. 2 Chr. 28:3. & 33:6. the children of both sexes are mentioned, as here, so Ps. 106:38. the more to aggravate the immanity of these unnatural miscreants, whom neither the dearness of the one, nor the tenderness of the other, their own bowels both, (as Paul of Onesimus, Philem. 12.) could move unto mercy, or withhold from exercising such cruelty on them. This inhumane practice they learned from those heathen, whom God had cast out before them, Deut. 12:31. and from those that succeeded the Israelites in Samaria, 2 Kings 17:31, 41. Concerning the manner of acting this hideous rite the Jewish writers relate many things; but their relations seem much of them rather fable than story: and I therefore let them pass.

*{which I commanded them not}* Or, *which I never commanded*: but expressly forbade, and professed to abhor, Lev. 18:21. & 20:3. Deut. 12:31. & 18:10.

*{neither came it into mine heart.}* Heb. *neither came it upon mine heart*; neither had I ever any the least thought so to do. See ch. 3:16.

**Verse 32.** *{Therefore behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that it shall no more be called Tophet, or the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter; for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place.}* See the same, ch. 19:6. That place, which is now so horribly abused, shall be so filled with the carcasses of slaughtered persons, that there shall not be room enough to afford them all burial, but they shall, many of them, lie rotting there above ground; and the valley shall have a new name given it from the multitude of those slaughtered bodies, that shall, partly, be interred therein, and partly, lie there unburied.

*{behold, the days come}* Heb. *behold, the days coming*; as Isa. 39:6. ch. 9:24.

*{it shall no more be called Tophet, or the valley of the son of Hinnom}* Not that it should not at all be so named any more, or known by either of those names (for unto this day the name continues) but that another name should be given it, that might as well, or much better, be used of it, than either of those two. See the like, Gen. 32:28. ch. 20:3.

*{the valley of slaughter}* Or, *Ge-haharegah*; as Judas his field was called *Akeldama*, Acts 1:19. Howbeit, some by *slaughter* here, understand *slaughtered ones*; which the article prefixed, seems to back: and they render it therefore *the valley of the slaughtered*; for the meaning is not, that the slaughter of them should be made there; but that either their slaughtered bodies, for burial, should be brought, there being no place readier, or fitter, at hand, to receive them.

*{for they shall bury in Tophet}* Heb. *and*; but, *for*, here; as ch. 5:2. because a reason is rendered, why the name before mentioned should be given unto it.

*{till there be no place}* Or, *because there is no place*, or *no room*; to wit, to bury elsewhere. Heb. *for no place being*; that is, *for want of room*; all wonted places of burial, being so glutted with corpses, that they are able to receive no more: for the particle is oft used in a causal notion; as ch. 4:6. & 10:6. & 19:11.

**Verse 33.** *{And the carcasses of this people, shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.}* They shall lie unburied, and be devoured by birds and beasts, either for want of persons to bury them, or for want of places to bury them in: so Ps. 79:2, 3. ch. 24:20. See the same, ch. 19:7.

*{carcasses}* Heb. *carcass*: but taken collectively; as Isa. 9:28. & 26:19. and so *fowl*, and *beast*.

*{heaven}* Or, *air*; as it is rendered, Ps. 8:8. Deut. 28:26.

*{and none shall fray them away.}* Either for fear of the enemy, or by reason of the great devastation that shall be, and want of persons to look after them, and inter them. So Deut. 28:26. a defect of the pronoun, in this form of speech perpetual; as Isa. 17:2. ch. 30:10. & 46:27. Ezek. 34:28. Mic. 4:4. Nah. 2:11. as if it were said, *there shall be no frighter*.

**Verse 34.** *{Then will I cause to cease from the cities of Judah, and from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride:}* I will bereave them of all matter that people are wont to rejoice in, or to make themselves merry with. So Isa. 24:7, 8. ch. 16:9. & 25:10. & 33:11. Ezek. 26:13. Hos. 2:11. Rev. 8:23.

*{Then}* Or, *thus*. Heb. *And*; as Isa. 19:22.

*{the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride}* Such merry songs, and melodious music, as at weddings is wont to be, Ps. 78:63.

*{for the land shall be desolate}* Heb. *unto desolation*; as Isa. 64:11. so ch. 25:11.

## CHAPTER 8

**Verse 1.** *{At that time, saith the LORD, they shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of the princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem out of their graves,}* That this chapter has coherence with the former, is apparent by the very words of it. In it the prophet proceeds to show the grievous calamities that should befall this people, with whom the enemy should spare neither living nor dead, but wreak their rage upon either, vv. 1, 3. complains of their extreme stupidity and obstinacy in evil, vv. 4, 12. threatens them with utter and unavoidable destruction, verses 10, 13, 16, 17. and bewails their forlorn and incurable condition, vv. 14, 16, 18, 22.

*{At that time}* When those days are come, whereof ch. 7:32.

*{they shall bring out the bones}* The enemy, either for greediness of gain, or in extremity of despite, shall even rifle their graves, and not suffer their bodies, or their bones to rest in them. A further addition to what was before denounced, that they should not only want room to bury their slain, ch. 7:32. but those also that were already buried, should be plucked out of their graves again. See Baruch 2:24.

*{of the kings of Judah, and of his princes}* In whose sepulchers, it is not unlikely, that they looked for rich ornaments and jewels, or treasure: see Joseph the Jew in his *Antiquities, l. 13. c. 15.*

*{of the priests, and of the prophets,}* Those especially are here aimed at, that had been corrupt priests, and false prophets. See the like in some kind, through the just judgment of God, both denounced and executed upon the like, 1 Kings 13:2. 2 Kings 23:14, 20.

*{of the inhabitants}* See this judgment in the like manner promiscuously threatened, Lev. 26:30.

**Verse 2.** *{And they shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and after whom they have walked, and whom they have sought, and whom they have worshipped.}* And so made idols of them, committing idolatry, that is, spiritual adultery with them, preferring the creature before the Creator, Deut. 4:19. 2 Kings 23:5. 2 Chr. 33:5. ch. 7:18. Ezek. 8:16. their bones should be laid before these creatures of God's making, whom they had abused to idolatry, as their carcasses were laid and burnt upon the altars of their own making, Lev. 26:30. 2 Kings 23:14, 20. as in a way of detestation on the one, so in way of demonstration also to the other; thereby showing how little good either the one, or the other, could do them, being unable to safeguard them, either alive, or dead.

*{before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven}* That is, the stars, 2 Kings 23:5. implying that they should lie night and day unburied; as of Jehoiakim's carcass, ch. 36:30.

*{they shall not be gathered, nor buried, they shall be for dung upon the face of the earth}* They shall not be gathered to be laid up in the monuments of their ancestors; nor obtain so much as common sepulture: so some. But the words seem to be intended rather, in a larger, and more indefinite sense either of them: for bones thus scattered, must of necessity be gathered, ere they can be interred anywhere: the meaning is, they shall lie above ground till they rot. So Ps. 83:10. ch. 9:22. & 16:4.

**Verse 3.** *{And death shall be chosen rather than life, of all the residue of them that remain of all this evil family, which remain in all the places whither I have driven them, saith the LORD.}* Or, *in all the places of the remaining ones*, (so the words run) *whither I shall have driven them*. Though the cruelty of the barbarous enemy be such, as that they spared neither living nor dead, but massacred the one, and digged up the other; yet so great shall be the calamities, and so miserable the condition of those that survive, and are carried away captive, that being weary of their lives, they shall wish that they had died with the rest of their people, that had perished either during the siege, or in the surprisal of the city; and counted them happy that so did. See Lev. 26:36, 39. Job 3:20, 21. & 7:15. 1 Kings 19:4. Rev. 9:6. & 14:13.

**Verse 4.** *{Moreover, thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the LORD;}* Heb. *And*: as ch. 1:11. To manifest the equity of God's proceeding thus in severity with them, he does in the words following, describe their extreme folly, and willful obstinacy, running on headlong with an utter refusal to be stopped or stayed on the way, unto those courses that tend to their utter ruin and destruction.

*{Shall they fall, and not arise?}* Or, *when men fall, will they not rise?* See the like syntax, ch. 6:9, 10. & 7:27. Is there any man so absurd and witless, who when he has by accident got a fall, will lie still, and not assay to get up again? or that will refuse to be holpen up again, by such as offer him their help? Eccl. 4:10. Hereby intimating the folly of this people, that having fallen by, and for their sin, Hos. 14:1. yet refused to rise, or to be raised again by those, that took pains with them to that purpose. Some render the words, *are they so fallen, that they cannot rise again?* do they deem their case desperate? See ch. 2:25. But the former seems the proper sense of the place.

*{shall he turn away, and not return}* Or, *will not one that hath turned aside*, or, *gone aside, return?* Will not any man that has gone unwillingly out of the way, desire to come into it again; and be willing to receive direction from those, that would set him again in it? See the application of it to this people, v. 5. For those, either of the Jewish, or ours, that render it; *if he did return, would not God return?* as if he should say, undoubtedly he would, ch. 3:1. Zech. 1:3. make a needless insertion, and seem to go beside the scope of the place.

**Verse 5.** *{Why then is this people of Jerusalem slidden back, by a perpetual backsliding.}* Heb. *why is this people*, (not, *of Jerusalem*; for the word *people* here, is entire and absolute, but either) *in Jerusalem*, (as the old Latin) or, *Jerusalem*, (by way of apposition) *revolted*, or, *gone aside* (for the verb is feminine, as answering not to *people*, but to *Jerusalem*, as the like, Judg. 18:7. and is the same word, with that in the former branch, though in another form) *by a perpetual*, or, *a pertinacious revolt*, or, *aversion*: and to little purpose does a learned man trouble himself, and torture the text, because he finds the participle used actively, Isa. 47:10. to have the words rendered, *Jerusalem* (that is, the rulers of it) *misleadeth this people*; or, *a pertinacious aversion leadeth this people away*: when as he may find the participle, or participial at least, so oft elsewhere in a passive or neuter notion; for, *refractory*, or, *rebellious*, Isa. 57:17. ch. 3:14, 22. & 31:22. & 49:4. and the meaning is plain enough. What is the reason then, that this people contrary to the usual manner of men in such case, having gone out of the right way, and being in a wrong way, prejudicial to themselves, yet will pertinaciously thus persist, and go on in the same, and refuse to be reduced? ch. 2:26. & 5:3. and 9:16.

*{they hold fast deceit, they refuse to return}* Or, carrying on the sentence in one tenor with the former; *do they hold fast deceit? do they refuse to return?* more fully thus: *Why is it, that this people do thus pertinaciously persist in their going aside*, or, *revolt, that they hold fast deceit? that they refuse to return?* where by *deceit*, some understand their unjust and fraudulent courses, which were exceeding rife among them, ch. 9:6. Mic. 6:10. & 7:5. See Ps. 36:3. & 55:11. Others rather, those frauds and falsehoods, wherewith their false prophets deceived and deluded them, ch. 5:31. & 14:14. & 23:26. Isa. 30:10. See 2 Thess. 2:10, 12.

**Verse 6.** *{I hearkened and heard; but they spake not aright.}* The most interpreters, both Jewish and others, conceive these words to be the prophet's, relating how he had observed it to be with the people; as ch. 6:27, 29. I suppose them rather to be the speech of God himself, implying as his long expectation and forbearance, so his earnest and longing desire of their repentance, expressed by a phrase borrowed from the practice of men, who are wont diligently and constantly to listen after that, which they much desire to hear. See Ps. 85:8. Isa. 50:4. See of God the like, Mal. 3:16. See also 1 Kings 20:33.

*{I hearkened and heard}* Or, *I have listed to hear*; as, *arose and warred*, for, *arose to war*, Josh. 24:9. for he could hear nothing of that which he desired to hear.

*{they spake not aright}* Or, *none spake aright*; as the word is used, 2 Kings 7:9. Eccl. 8:10. ch. 23:10. or, as the Greek renders it, *none so spake*: so the word is most commonly taken, Exod. 10:11. Deut. 18:14. Ps. 1:4. in such manner, as men would do in the cases before mentioned, verse 4.

*{no man repented of his wickedness, saying, what have I done?}* Heb. *there is not a man* (as ch. 5:1.) *repenting of his wickedness*; as, *to say, what have I done?* that has any remorse, or touch at all in his conscience, for any of his sins so far forth, as but to think once seriously with himself, what it was that he had therein done; that which they were exhorted to do, ch. 2:23.

*{what have I done?}* The manner of a man's speech or thought, recollecting himself after some sudden and inconsiderate act: so Samuel to Saul, 1 Sam. 13:11. and Joab to David; *what hast thou done?* 2 Sam. 3:24.

*{every one turned to his course}* Or, *each one of them turneth to their course*, or, *race*; to his *evil course*, or, *race*: as it is, ch. 23:10. it implies their eagerness in the pursuit of evil; so Isa. 59:7. Prov. 6:18.

*{as an horse rusheth into the battle}* Heb. *like an horse rushing into the war*: the word rendered, *rushing*, is very emphatic; for it signifies properly an *inundation* of waters, with much violence breaking in, and overflowing all before it, Isa. 8:9. & 28:15, 18. ch. 47:2. *war*, for, *battle*, as 2 Sam. 18:6, 8. They run headlong after their own lusts and fancies, and will not be curbed or restrained of them: like a headstrong horse, that hearing the noise of the trumpet, and smelling the battle afar off, does with much violence in a full career, make towards it; his rider having now no command of him, nor being able to keep him in; see Job 39:21, 25. and of this people's unbridled, untamable, and untractable disposition, ch. 2:23, 24.

**Verse 7.** *{Yea, the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed time, and the turtle, and the crane, and the swallow, observe the time of their coming, but my people know not the judgment of the LORD.}* In these words is reproved, not their obstinacy only and willfulness, but their stupidity and blockishness, wherein they came short even of the unreasonable creatures; whereof divers sorts here mentioned, do duly observe the times of their coming, and going from place to place, from one region to another, according to the season of the year, Job 39:26. whereas this sottish people, had not so much wit as to take notice of, and observe God's courses and dealings with them; of the seasons of grace, when in mercy he offers himself unto them; or of the times of wrath, wherein he shows himself displeased with them; to lay hold on and embrace the one, and to seek to prevent and stay the proceeding of the other, Isa. 55:12. ch. 5:4. Luke 12:56. & 19:42, 44. See the like exprobration of stupidity, and sottishness in God's people, Isa. 1:3.

*{yea}* Heb. *also*; so ch. 5:28.

*{the stork}* The fowl here mentioned is ranked among the unclean ones, Lev. 11:19. Deut. 14:18. where some render it a *kite*; and the Jewish doctors some of them tell us, that it is a kind of *white kite*, or, *puttock*: some, an *hern*; because it is said to build in the *fir trees*, Ps. 107:14. Some would have it to be the *ostrich*, grounded on that place, Job 39:13, 14. where she is said as they suppose, to leave her eggs in the sand, where by the heat of the sun, they are hatched; but if the text be duly weighed, it will be found, that this fowl, whatever it be, and the ostrich, are there distinguished: see the note on the place. That it is a fowl of large wings, it is apparent from Zech. 5:9. and that it is one of those, that change their quarters at time of year, is no less apparent from this place. The most therefore, among whom divers of the Jewish writers, take it for a *stork*, which breeds also, says one of the Jewish masters, as well in high trees, as in lofty turrets, that which those must do of necessity, that live in the woody wastes where no housing is. That the *stork*, as well as the *crane*, changes his quarters, authors generally agree. See Aristotle in his *story of living wights, l. 8. c. 16.* and Pliny in his *natural history*,

*l. 10. c. 23.* save that Pliny says, that the one comes against summer, and goes away against winter; the other comes against winter, and goes away against summer; and seems of the stork to affirm this latter, which is certainly untrue: and Ælian, they go and come together. It is deemed in Hebrew, to have its name from a term that signifies *piety*, or kindness; and this fowl, say the Jewish critics, is so called, because he parts his prey among his companions: but others, because they are reported to feed their parents, when through age they grow impotent. Hereof Aristotle l. 9. c. 13. Pliny also where before. Ælian l. 3. c. 23. Aristophanes the comic in his *birds*: and others, not a few; and among the Greeks a proverbial term, denoting this duty in children towards parents, is in very frequent use. Howbeit, I suppose rather, that this name was at first given unto this fowl, in regard of her tender affection to her young; whereof divers examples have been in the Netherlands, (where I have also seen of them, on their nests on the housetop) and among others of some, that have either burnt themselves, to save their young; or together with them, when they could not save them, the houses being fired on which their nests were. See Adrian Yong in his *Batavia*, for how either they should come, to know their sires or dams again, when they are grown old; or it should come to be observed of them, how they then tend them as of their young it may well be, is neither of them easy to conceive.

*{in the heaven}* What the rabbin hence gathers concerning this fowl, that it should be a great fowl, and of high flight; as the like therefore is said of the eagle, Prov. 23:5. & 30:19. is frivolous, since all *birds* in general, are called *birds of the heaven*, Ps. 8:8. and *heaven* both here and elsewhere, is no other than the *air*, see ch. 7:33.

*{knoweth}* Observes as duly as if she knew. So Ps. 104:19. Job 38:12.

*{his appointed time}* His set season of coming and going.

*{and the turtle}* Whose access shows the spring's approach, Cant. 2:12. See Aristotle, l. 8. c. 3, 12, 16. Varro of *husbandry*, l. 3. c. 5.

*{the crane and the swallow}* Or, *the swallow and the crane*; of the terms, see on Isa. 38:14. of the cranes coming and going; see before with the *stork*; of the *swallows* the Greek proverb is well known, being grown as familiar with us, as with them, that *One swallow maketh not a summer*.

*{but}* Heb. *and*: as ch. 7:24.

*{my people know not the judgment of the LORD.}* See ch. 5:4, 5. *judgment*, for, *course*, or, *manner* of dealing; as 1 Sam. 2:13. & 8:11. thus man who should be wiser than the fowls of the air, Job 35:11. seems to come short herein of them, in things so nearly concerning him.

**Verse 8.** *{How do ye say, we are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us?}* Or, *How can ye say* (as ch. 2:23.) *We are wise*: the pronoun demonstrative, includes the verb substantive; so Isa. 19:11. How have you the face to arrogate wisdom to yourselves, when you are more sottish and senseless, than the very brute creatures themselves, verse 7.

*{the law of the LORD is with us}* We have the law of God with us, have been trained up in it, and are well acquainted with it, and are not therefore such silly sots, as you would make us to be: as they presumed much of the temple, ch. 7:4. so they vaunted much of the law, ch. 18:18. Rom. 2:17, 18. as if the having of the law among them, were enough to make them a wise people, though they neither regarded it, nor walked according to the rules of it, Rom. 2:21, 23. This some suppose spoken to the priests, whose office it was to instruct the people out of the law, Deut. 33:10. Mal. 2:7. and it may well in special have an eye unto them: but it seems to be more large, as the charge is more general, both here, v. 7. and before, ch. 5:4, 5. as also Isa. 1:3.

*{lo certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribe is in vain.}* *In vain hath he* (that is, God; the pronoun for the noun, as Exod. 34:28. 1 Sam. 6:19.) *made it*; a defect of the pronoun, as ch. 4:4. or the verb being taken indefinitely, *in vain was it*; (to wit, the law) *made, in vain*; as the word is used, 1 Sam. 25:21. ch. 5:23. for they that render it, *in vain hath he* (that is, the writer) *prepared his pen*, regard not the pauses in the Hebrew text. Now according to this version the meaning is, that the law was in vain enacted by God, or by his appointment put in writing by scribes thereunto designed for the use and benefit of his people, Deut. 17:18. and 31:9. in regard of any use that they made of it, or benefit that thence redounded to them by it, because it was by them no whit regarded, Hos. 8:12. and thus do the Jewish commenters some of them expound it, whom divers of ours therein concur with. Howbeit, the old Latin after the Greek, and the Chaldee, which some other of the rabbins agree with; and not a few of ours follow, understand this passage as spoken of the wicked scribes, that misexpounded the law, perverting and wresting it, to please the humors of the people, and sided with the false prophets, whom they adhered to, and approved; and to this effect they render the words: *Lo, surely the deceitful*, or, *lying, pen*, or, *quill, of the scribes, worketh for falsehood*, or, *dealeth deceitfully*: Heb. *the quill*, or, *pen*; for it is properly a pen made of the quill of some *fowl*, of the bigger sort especially, such as are used to prey, Gen. 15:11. 1 Sam. 14:33. Isa. 46:11. ch. 12:9. though used more generally for any kind of *pen*, Ps. 45:2. or, *style*, though of metal, Job 19:24. ch. 17:1. and, *the quill*; or, *pen of falsehood*, for, *a false quill*, or, *pen*: as, *a tongue of falsehood*, for, *a false tongue*, Prov. 26:28. that tells lies the one, that writes lies the other: *of the scribes*; such as were to interpret the law, Ezra 7:6. but dealt corruptly and falsely with it, Matt. 23:15. Luke 11:51. Heb. *doth to falsehood*; as, *to swear to falsehood*, Lev. 6:3. ch. 5:2. or, *doth falsehood*; as, *to do truth*, for, *to deal truly*, 1 John 1:6. so, *to do falsehood*, for, *to deal falsely*; for the particle is oft redundant; as Gen. 2:24. compared with Matt. 19:5, 6. Ezek. 37:27. with 2 Cor. 6:16. 1 Kings 19:18, 20. See Ps. 94:20. Isa. 10:1. either version may well be admitted, in regard of the terms; but the former seems the genuine.

**Verse 9.** *{The wise men are ashamed, they are dismayed and taken}* That is, as some, the wisest among them, may well be ashamed of their gross ignorance, and folly, vv. 7, 8. Rom. 1:22. or, as others rather, *The wise men shall be confounded*; and all their wisdom shall not avail, to keep them from being dismayed, confounded, and captivated when the judgment now denounced shall be put in execution; see ch. 4:9. and 6:11. verse 12. So of Babel, Isaiah 47:10, 14. Howbeit, some of note read the words, by way of interrogation, and thus render; *Have these wise men, made the people to be ashamed*, (to wit, of their sins) *dismayed*, (with fear of God's wrath) *and taken*, with remorse, and repentance, and so brought home to God? But this reading strains the words of the text overmuch; nor is the first word, though the form be such, found but once only in an active notion, and the other two not at all: of the first, see on ch. 6:15. of the last, on ch. 6:11.

*{lo they have rejected the word of the LORD,}* Which yet they so much vaunt of, v. 8. See ch. 6:10, 19.

*{and what wisdom is in them?}* Or, *what wisdom then have they?* Heb. *and the wisdom of what is to them*: *and*, for, *then*; as ch. 4:1. what wisdom can they have, who reject that wherein all true wisdom consists? Deut. 4:6. Ps. 19:7. & 119:130. Prov. 2:6. 2 Tim. 3:15.

**Verse 10.** *{Therefore will I give their wives unto others, and their fields to them that shall inherit them}* See on ch. 6:11.

*{therefore}* This term may have reference, either to their rejection of God's law, mentioned v. 9. or, to those vices afterward charged on them in this verse.

*{will I give their wives unto others}* Put them into the power of strangers, as 2 Sam. 12:11, 12.

*{to them that shall inherit them}* Heb. *to possessors*, to strangers *that shall possess* them; or, *possess themselves* of them: the word *strangers* supplied from the former branch, as Isa. 10:5. & 48:13. and a defect of the pronoun, as Ezek. 7:25.

*{for every one, from the least even to the greatest, is given to covetousness; from the prophet, even to the priest, every one dealeth falsely}* Or, *because*, etc. See the same passage. Ch. 5:13.

**Verse 11.** *{For they have healed the hurt of my people slightly, saying, peace, peace, when there is no peace}* Heb. *and they heal*, or, *cure*, etc. See the same before, ch. 6:14.

**Verse 12.** *{Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush; therefore shall they fall among them that fall, in the time of their visitation, they shall be cast down, saith the LORD.}* See the same, ch. 6:15.

**Verse 13.** *{I will surely consume them, saith the LORD}* Or, *utterly consume them*: Heb. *Gathering, I will gather them*, or, *consuming, I will consume them*: for those two roots, come very near the one to the other, and roots so near in their several forms, are oft confounded: for it is against the usual manner of the tongue in such forms as this, to have the words in two several notions; the verb infinitive in one, and the finite in another. See the like denunciation, Zeph. 1:2, 3.

*{there shall be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade, and the things that I have given them, shall pass away from them.}* All means of relief and sustenance, shall be taken away from them, in the time of the siege of the city. So Joel 1:7, 12. Hab. 3:17. the enemy having destroyed, and devoured all before them, v. 16. and he mentions these two, the *grape*, and the *fig*, says the rabbin, because these two among their fruits were of greatest reckoning, and most general use in those parts, see Isa. 36:16. ch. 5:17.

*{and the leaf shall fade}* Or, *fall*, rather; see Isa. 1:30. being together with the fruit beaten down, before the usual time of shedding. Howbeit, some read the words, as spoken by way of similitude, (as some of our versions do the like, Ps. 48:7.) thus rendering the text; *I will utterly consume them, as when no grapes are on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf is shed*: as when, with some sore tempest, both vine and fig tree are so smitten, that there is neither fruit, nor leaf left on them, Ps. 78:47. And this should I prefer before that which some other of prime note exhibit; rendering the words, *there is no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, yea, the leaves are fallen*; that is, there is no fruit of good works to be found among them; as Isaiah 5:2. nor so much as any show of such, neither fruit, nor leaf; it is worse with them, than with that fig tree, Matt. 21:19. Luke 13:6. But I adhere, to that which our version has, though the second be not improbable.

*{and the things that I have given them, shall pass away from them.}* They shall be deprived of those fruits of the earth, and other the like commodities, which I had formerly in great abundance bestowed upon them, Hos. 2:8, 9. according to this reading, there is a defect in the text, both of the antecedent and the relative; as ch. 2:8. and the preposition is included in the verb; as Job 29:3. ch. 10:25. Howbeit, the Chaldee, which some of the Jewish commenters, the old Latin, and divers others of ours also follow, understand it of the people's transgressions of God's law; and render the words: some of them, *and the precepts that I gave them they have transgressed them*: as an addition to what was said concerning their want of fruit and leaf. Others, *because* (the copulative for the causal, as ch. 6:29, 32.) *they have transgressed them*, or, *those things*, (that is, the laws; the pronoun for the noun, as Isa. 33:2.) *that I gave to them*: a defect of the relative; as ch. 6:15, 20. So it should render a reason of the foregoing denunciation. See the like, Isa. 24:4, 5. And this seems very probable: more probable at least, than that of some other, *whatsoever I use about them passeth away*; there comes nothing of all the care, pains, and cost taken about them; it is all but lost labor, ch. 2:30. for how the words of the text will admit this, I see not: or, (as I suppose) than that of another, *I gave them those things*, (to wit, the fruits before mentioned; not that they should enjoy them, but) *that they should pass away from them*; and leave them destitute: and no marvel therefore, if they be all gone.

**Verse 14.** *{Why do we sit still? assemble yourselves; and let us enter into the defenced cities; and let us be silent there.}* A speech conceived, as in the person of the people, inciting one another, upon notice of the enemies' approach, with all speed, to betake themselves for shelter and safeguard unto the places of greatest strength and surety. See the like before, ch. 4:5, 6.

*{Why do we sit still?}* Heb. *for what*; in, *Upon what are we sitting?* as reproving one another, that they made no more haste: and demanding, what they stayed consulting upon; or what succor other ways they could expect. See Matt. 24:16, 18.

*{assemble yourselves}* Or, *retire ye*. See on ch. 4:6.

*{defenced cities}* Heb. *cities of defense*, or, *fortification*; as Isa. 36:1. ch. 5:17.

*{let us be silent}* Heb. *quiet*; as Isa. 62:7. Lam. 3:28. as if they should say; it is in vain for us to stir, or conceive hope to be able to do ought against so potent an enemy; and our wisest course therefore, is to betake ourselves to some such place, and to keep ourselves quiet there.

*{for the LORD our God hath put us to silence;}* These words some make the speech of the prophet, in way of answer to the former speech of the people: and they read the words; *Surely* (as Exod. 3:12. Isa. 63:16.) *the Lord our God hath put us to silence*; that is, say they, has stopped our mouths, that we should not complain of the wrongs done us by the Chaldean forces. See Lam. 3:26, 29, 39. Ps. 39:9. But the most rather conceive them as the words of the people, beginning at length to see a hand of God in those things that befell them, and concluding therefore that it was in vain for them to assay to make head against the Chaldeans; as the Egyptians, Exod. 14:25. *for*, or, *since that*, (as ch. 10:7.) say they, *the Lord our God* (he who had wont to be our protector, and encourager) *hath put us to silence*; that is, has now withdrawn himself, and so taken our courage away from us, that we dare not so much as open our mouths against the enemy, much less to lift up hand against him. See Exod. 11:7. Josh. 10:21. Ps. 38:13, 14. And this seems to be the genuine sense of the place. However we take it, there is an elegant antanaclasis, or variety of notion, in the term; as if he had said, It is best for to get us into some strong city, and be quiet there; for God has struck us with astonishment, and made us as mute, or as still, as a stone. See Exod. 15:15, 16.

*{and hath given us waters of gall to drink;}* So is the word rendered, Ps. 69:21. Deut. 29:18. where yet it may seem not so proper to say, *a root bearing gall*: *grapes of gall*, for, *grapes as bitter as gall*; may seem more tolerable, Deut. 32:32. but that also comes short of what is there intended; to wit, not *bitter* barely, but *venomous*, or, *poisonous grapes*: for in the next words, verse 33. it is said of the wine that comes of them, it is as the *venom*, or *poison, of asps*: from which place some of the Jewish critics gather, that it is a kind of poison that lies in the *head* of the asp, and thence has its name; but other of them, that it is the *gall* of the asp: and to reconcile these two, some further affirm, that there are certain veins reaching from the gall of the asp, unto her mouth, by which the poison, when she is angered, is conveyed to the one from the other: but these are things uncertain. One of the Jewish commenters well renders it here, *a cup of death*, or *deadly poison*; and withal tells us, that it is the name of a poisonful herb, or plant, wherewith they use to poison and kill people: and that it is indeed some such herb or plant, appears plainly by Hos. 10:4. where it is said *to grow in the furrows*, or, *ridges, of the field*: such was the *cicuta*, or, *hemlock*, at Athens, with the juice whereof, they used to put condemned persons there to death. Whence that saying by some used of Socrates, who so suffered death, dying with much confidence and courage, that *hemlock made him a great man*; as being made more famous by his death, than his life: and *aconitum*, or, *wolfsbane*, in much use and note for wicked practices in that kind: in regard whereof, as the name *aconitum*, is more at large both in Greek and Latin writers, used for *rank poison* in general: so the name of this *rosh* (for so it is termed in Hebrew) is used in Scripture more generally for any kind of venom or poison whatsoever. By *waters* therefore, or *juice, of rosh*, that is, of *hemlock, wolfsbane*, or the like, wherewith God is said here to have *drenched* this people, is imported those grievous afflictions and calamities, tending even to death and destruction, that God had brought upon them for their sins. So ch. 9:15. & 23:15. Lam. 3:19.

*{because we have sinned against the LORD.}* The cursed root from whence all these poisonful fruits spring, Lam. 3:39, 42. and 5:16.

**Verse 15.** *{We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of health, and behold trouble}* Heb. *Looking we looked* (of which kind of speech, see on Isa. 59:13. we looked long, till our eyes failed us, Lam. 4:17.) *and* (as verse 7.) *good was not; for a time of healing, and behold trouble*, or *terror*; as Job 6:4. Ps. 88:16. our prophets ceased not to put us in expectation of peace and safety, and bare us still in hand that all should be well, and that all the evils we feared, would be easily helped and healed, v. 11. but we see nothing less, no good, but all evil, matter of consternation, trouble and terror. See the same, ch. 14:19. yet some would have them the words of the prophet to the people, reading the text thus, *Look for peace, but* there will be *no good; for a time of remedy*, but *behold* it will prove *trouble*. But the former follows more smoothly from the context, and the terms of it; as also, the parallel place confirms it.

**Verse 16.** *{The snorting of his horses was heard from Dan, the whole land trembled at the sound of the neighing of the strong ones; for they are come, and have devoured the land, and all that is in it, the city and those that dwell therein.}* The noise of the Chaldean forces, entered upon the land, of their cavalry especially, is heard far and near, and makes all to tremble; for they spoil and destroy all before them, as well in city as country.

*{snorting}* The former versions had it *neighing*; but that follows after; and this, and that, in propriety of speech, are two distinct and diverse things: for that which is rendered *neighing* in the words following, is that noise, properly, which horses make, when they are frolic, or when they look after the mare, or miss some of their company, that they use to keep with: of which, see ch. 5:8. and this proceeds by the mouth: whereas that here rendered *snorting*, and the rabbins express by a word that signifies *neesing*, (from which yet it much differs) is the noise that they make, when they are held in, or are chased; so called, because it passes through the *nostrils*, Job 39:20. *the glory of his nostrils is terrible*; or, of *his snorting*, as some there render it; and of the *Leviathan*, Job 40:20. *out of his nostrils goeth smoke*: both words are here used to comprehend whatsoever dreadful noises horses are wont to make, either in their march, or in the field, and withal, such hideous noises, as so numerous an army would fill the air with. Isa. 13:4.

*{of his horses}* Of the enemies, the Chaldeans, ch. 4:13. and 6:23.

*{was heard}* Or, *is heard*: either the noise itself, or the report of it, ch. 6:24.

*{from Dan}* Through which Nebuchadnezzar, having subdued Phoenicia, marched toward Judah and Jerusalem. See ch. 4:15.

*{the whole land trembled}* Or, *trembleth*, ch. 6:24.

*{the neighing}* See *snorting* before.

*{of his strong ones}* So the Chaldee understanding it of his mighty and valiant men; and the old Latin, *of his warriors*: but the word of *neighing*, though metaphorically attributed to lustful wantons, ch. 5:8. will not well agree to men here: it does evidently answer to the word *horses* beforegoing, and may well be rendered *steeds*; or more fully, *stout*, or *sturdy steeds*: for that is the commendation of such, and the word does properly signify, the *prime, chief, choice*, or excellent in each kind; used of *men*, whom valor and courage commends, Job 24:22. & 34:20. (see Isa. 46:12.) of *angels*, whom might and excellency, Ps. 78:25. of *bulls*, whom fatness and bulk of body, Ps. 22:12. & 50:13. & 68:30. Isa. 34:7. ch. 50:11. of *horses* and *steeds*, whom stoutness of stomach, Judg. 5:22. ch. 47:3. and so here: it is in the singular number used very frequently of God. See Isa. 1:24.

*{for they are come}* They are entered the country. Heb. *and they are come*; as ch. 6:29, 32.

*{and have devoured the land all that is in it}* Or, *do devour*; or eat up and destroy. Heb. *the land and the fullness of it*; as Ps. 24:1. See ch. 4:20. & 5:17.

*{the city and those that dwell therein}* That is, as some, Jerusalem with her inhabitants, ch. 4:29. but I suppose rather, that the word *city* is here taken collectively; *city*, for, *cities*; as Isa. 27:10. as if he had said, city and country are alike before them, they spoil, plunder, and destroy all alike: or if we understand it of Jerusalem, it must be rendered, as some also do, *for they are come to destroy the land, and all that is in it, the city, and those that dwell therein.* See the like syntax, verse 6.

**Verse 17.** *{For behold, I will send serpents, cockatrice among you, which will not be charmed; and they shall bite you, saith the LORD.}* Heb. *behold, I am sending* (as ch. 29:17.) *among you serpents, cockatrices*, (by way of apposition: of which kind of serpent, see on Isa. 11:8. & 14:29.) *whom there shall be no charm for them*; an elegant redundancy in that language very frequent, as Ps. 1:4. & 144:8. that is, *for whom there shall be no charm*: of the use of charms, to prevent stinging by serpents, see Ps. 58:4, 5. Eccl. 10:11. for absurdly does a writer of ours allege this place, to prove that there is no such thing: and as well might he allege Exod. 22:18. to prove that there are no *witches*, the main scope of his work: for as God there forbidding *to suffer a witch to live*, does presume that such there were; so when he threatens to send serpents that shall not be charmed, he does imply, that such sometime were charmed, though not indeed by any intrinsical virtue, or natural power in the spell or charm, or the terms used in it, but by the act of Satan subtly cooperating with it: the *serpents* here menaced to be sent in among them, are the Chaldeans, whose cruelty they should by no means be able to mitigate. See ch. 4:25. 2 Chr. 36:17.

*{and they shall bite you}* There is an elegant consonancy in the original, between the word that signifies a *serpent*, and this of *biting*, differing but in a letter, and that also of a near sound, the one from the other; which our English cannot express; but hereby it appears, that the kind of serpents here alluded to, is not of those that have their sting in the tail; as the *scorpion*, Rev. 9:10. but that have their venom in or about their teeth; as asps and vipers, and our adders and snakes.

**Verse 18.** *{When I would comfort myself against sorrow, my heart is faint in me.}* After God's menacing speech, verse 17. the prophet's words professing his exceeding great and continual sorrow for the woeful condition of his people, of which he was by no means able to ease himself, though he had assayed sometime so to do. See the like, Isa. 22:4. Heb. as some, *O thou that refreshest me*, or *shouldest refresh me against grief*, or *amidst grief*; that is, say they, my soul. Others, *when my soul is*, or *would be refreshing itself*, or *refresheth me*, (as some) *my heart fainteth within me*; a defect of the particle of time; as Isa. 17:6. & 26:10. and the word *soul* supplied, because the term is feminine; as, the word, *preacher*, Eccl. 1:1. See ch. 4:19. yet some make the word to be, not a participle, but a noun, rendering it, *my recreation is joined with grief*: but the verb I find divers times used in Scripture, Job 9:27. & 10:20. Ps. 39:13. and the participle with the same syntax that here it has, Amos 5:9. but no such noun anywhere. And some would have it the speech of the people besieged in Jerusalem, and after long expectation of helps in vain fainting, Lam. 4:17. but this seems not so well to suit with the course of the context.

*{my heart is faint in me.}* Heb. *upon me*; as Ps. 143:4. See Lam. 1:22.

**Verse 19.** *{Behold, the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people because of them that dwell in a far country:}* The reason of this his sore grief, that he can have no ease of; because he seems to hear continually sounding in his ears, the lamentable shrieks and cries of his people, in their difficulties and distresses: see ch. 4:19. & 21:31.

*{the voice of the cry}* As, *the voice of my cry*, Ps. 5:2. *voice of cry*, for, *a loud cry*: as, *voice of report*, for, *a loud report*, ch. 10:22.

*{of the daughter of my people}* As ch. 4:11. & 6:26. So verse 21.

*{because of them that dwell in a far country}* By reason of the Chaldeans coming from a remote country, that grievously afflict and distress them. See ch. 5:15. & 6:22. Heb. *from the land of remotenesses*; which some therefore, with the old Latin, would have to be understood, of the people's bewailing their captivity in Babylon: but the particle here used, is very frequently a causal. So Ps. 12:5. Isa. 31:4. & 53:5. and so the rabbin here well renders it; for fear of the enemy coming from a remote land.

*{Is not the LORD in Zion? is not her king in her?}* These words, some would have to be the speech of God returned to the people, bewailing themselves in the time of their captivity; and demanding of them, as of Ahaziah, 2 Kings 1:3. whether there were no God in Israel, that he must needs send for an oracle to Beelzebub at Ekron; so whether they had not at Jerusalem God as a king to protect them, that they must needs send for King *Moloch* (so that idol's name signifies, whence the ambiguity, Zeph. 1:5.) to set him up in Tophet, and make him in the room of God their king, ch. 7:31. But the most, both Jewish, and others, expound them rather as the words of the people themselves, in their straits demanding in woeful wise, how it should come to pass, that the enemy should be able thus to prevail against Jerusalem: and some understand both branches of God; Has not God his seat at Jerusalem? and will he not, as their king, protect them and his own palace with them? See Ps. 44:4. & 48:2, 3. & 74:12. & 76:1, 2. Others, understand the former, of God; the latter, of their king; as if it were said, Have they neither God to save them, nor king to help them, that they are brought to such distress? See Hos. 10:3. & 13:10, 11.

*{why have they provoked me to anger with their graven images, and their strange vanities?}* These are, questionless, the words of God, returned to their expostulatory complaint, and rendering a reason why he had left them, and withdrawn the wing of his protection from them, and their city: to wit, for their leaving him, and betaking themselves to vain idols, ch. 2:11, 13. See ch. 5:19.

*{provoked me to anger}* Heb. *angered me*; as ch. 7:18, 19.

*{graven images}* Put here for all manner of idols; as Ps. 78:58. Isa. 42:8.

*{strange vanities}* Heb. *vanities* (so are idols termed, ch. 14:22.) *of a stranger*, that is, of a strange god; as Deut. 32:12. put collectively for *strange gods*; or, *of a strange people*; as Josh. 24:20. *the vanities of the heathen*, ch. 14:22.

**Verse 20.** *{The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.}* The speech of the people, again complaining that they had a long time looked for relief; but the year was gone, the time spent, within which they made full account to have had it, but none appeared. So verse 15. see ch. 37:7, 10. & 46:7, 8, 17. Lam. 4:17.

**Verse 21.** *{For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt, I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me.}* The prophet's words, again, lamenting the remediless afflictions of his people, and professing his sad and mournful affection for the same. Heb. *for the breach* (as v. 11.) *of the daughter of my people* (as v. 19.) *I am broken*: so, *my heart is broken*, ch. 23:9.

*{I am black}* Or, *I go in black*; as mourners are wont to do: I mourn, and am in heaviness, Ps. 38:6. ch. 14:2.

*{astonishment hath taken hold on me.}* While I consider the incurable condition of my people. See verse 22.
